LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 9 picks, including the Bills handing the Vikings their second straight loss Imagn Images The turnaround week looked promising early Sunday. Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3. As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take. Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track. Let's hope they bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 16 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Madrid on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain. Pick: Bengals 33, Falcons 21 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line. Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20 Dallas Cowboys (-6) at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game. Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17 New York Jets (+9.5) at Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around. Pick: Chiefs 24, Jets 17 Detroit Lions (-7) at Miami Dolphins This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff . Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13 Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints (-1.5) The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14 New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles (+3.5) The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late. Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20 Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders (+5.5) This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it. Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24 Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Texans are coming off a bye, while the Chargers are coming off a loss to the Rams. Neither team has come close to expectations before the season, with the Chargers winless. The Texans' defense and the Chargers' offense have both struggled. But I think the Chargers will hang around in this one behind their defense. Pick: Texans 19, Chargers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, while the 49ers are coming off a bye. Big edge for the 49ers. Plus, they are the better team. The Raiders' defense is struggling, so look for Brock Purdy to have a big day throwing the football. 49ers big. Pick: 49ers 31, Raiders 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (+3.5) This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses — even though both teams have good quarterbacks. The Packers have added rest from playing last Thursday, which will help. The Patriots had to rally and beat the Dolphins last week. The defenses play well, but It's Jordan Love who makes the plays late to win it. Pick: Packers 19, Patriots 16 Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks (-12.5) The Seahawks are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the Bears , while the Cardinals won at Dallas last week. They are making a quarterback change to Gardner Minshew , who played well last week. Good luck against this Seattle defense, which will be hunting after the Bears beat them. The Cardinals will get the brunt of their anger. Pick: Seahawks 30, Cardinals 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are coming off that impressive victory over Seattle Monday night on the road. That was domination. But there might be a little letdown here. The Bucs have played impressive defense this season and have cranked up their running game. They will run it well here, but in the end, Caleb Williams will make late plays to win it. Pick: Bears 24, Bucs 21 Buffalo Bills (-3.5) at Minnesota Vikings Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the game of the week, featuring two of the better teams in the league. I can't wait to see the Vikings ' defense against Josh Allen . But I think the Bills will run the ball at the Minnesota defense, much like the Lions did last week. The Bills defense has been better as of late, and that will show up against a limited Minnesota offense. That has put third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano in line to start in Week 9 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, which has caused a massive move in the odds. Sources: tests revealed that Ravens’ QB Tyler “Snoop” Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury. Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is out indefinitely with a thumb injury, Huntley’s season is over due to turf toe, and QB Joe Fagnano will start Thursday night vs. Jacksonville. pic.twitter.com/Cok4gbSvH3 Baltimore was favored in the lookahead line for this game before Week 8 with Jackson back in action, but the two-time league MVP was injured on the first offensive play for Baltimore and has since been ruled out for the next four weeks as he's set to go on injured reserve. So, the line re-opened with Jacksonville as a 7.5-point favorite on Sunday night. Now, that line has moved 2.5 more points with Huntley out and Fagnano (ankle) set to start. DraftKings Sportsbook has the Jaguars set as 10-point road favorites as they look to move to 6-2 this season. The Jaguars are very capable of blowing out bad teams, as they took down the Indianapolis Colts -- 42-7 -- in Week 8. Fagnano played a lot of Sunday's loss against the Buffalo Bills, completing 10 of his 21 pass attempts for 91 yards and a pick. He also had three carries for three yards and a fumble. The former UConn star is going to be in a tough spot against a Jacksonville team that is in the top-10 in the league in EPA/Play and success rate on defense while sporting the No. 1 run defense in the NFL. The Ravens (4-4) are major long shots to make the playoffs in the AFC, and there's a chance Jackson could end up missing the rest of the season if Baltimore is out of the mix by the time he's ready to return. Bettors that were able to grab the Jags early in the week certainly have to be happy, as it seems like this game is going to close with Trevor Lawrence and Co. favored by 10 or more points. The Jacksonville Jaguars are 8.5-point favorites as they visit the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 5, with kickoff set for 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. With the Ravens facing a full-blown quarterback disaster, my Jaguars vs. Ravens prediction and NFL picks are backing the visitors in what could be an absolute smackdown. TOP Pick Jaguars vs Ravens prediction: Jaguars -8.5 With rookie Joe Fagnano being the likely starter for the Baltimore Ravens , I'm expecting a bloodbath. Playable to -9.5. Fagnano completed just 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards against Buffalo and is now nursing an ankle injury on a short week. Baltimore hasn't topped 13 points in three straight games, sitting 30th in yards per play over that span . Meanwhile, the Jacksonville Jaguars ' offense is in a different galaxy right now, ranking third in yards per play over that stretch while scoring 73 points in its last two outings . The Ravens' defense has also been letting them down, allowing 71 points over its last two games. Isn't Jesse Minter supposed to be a defensive genius? Don't expect the Jaguars to play down to the competition. They're 12-3-1 ATS in their last 16 games as favorites, outscoring opponents by an average of 14 points and covering by an average of 8.6 points. Baltimore is 0-4-1 ATS in its last five games as a home underdog, losing by an average of 16 points. With the AFC's No. 1 seed to chase, Jacksonville has every reason to keep its foot on the gas. Jaguars vs Ravens combo Baltimore's quarterback situation might be the worst in the NFL. Playing on a short week against a Super Bowl contender makes matters even worse. Jacksonville has been an absolute bully against overmatched opponents , demolishing Indianapolis by 35 points as a 10.5-point favorite last week and smashing Cleveland by 24 as an 8.5-point favorite earlier this season. Let's pair another beatdown with a Brenton Strange touchdown. Baltimore has allowed a tight end to score in three of its last four games and has surrendered touchdowns on 83.3% of opponents' red-zone trips over its last three. This sets up beautifully for Strange to find the end zone in a Jacksonville rout. Brenton Strange anytime touchdown Jaguars vs Ravens touchdown scorer: Brenton Strange Baltimore's defense has been getting worked by tight ends, surrendering six touchdowns to the position this season . That's music to the ears of Strange, who's becoming a major piece of Jacksonville's passing attack. He's drawn at least seven targets in three of his last four games and enters Thursday as the Jaguars' second-most-targeted pass catcher this season. At just 28% on Kalshi, I'm buying the opportunity for Strange to find the end zone against this struggling defense. picks.blurb: Jaguars vs. Ravens bold predictions for Week 9 Thursday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Jaguars vs. Ravens bold predictions for Week 9 Thursday Night Football Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 10:16 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's a strange injury-marred matchup between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Baltimore Ravens . It's especially tough as the Ravens got hit at the QB position . But these teams meet in Week 9 on Thursday Night Football, and here are bold predictions. Life is better for the Jaguars. They're in the weaker AFC South division. They have a record of 5-2 and a three-game lead over the second-place Texans. Meanwhile, the Ravens are 4-4. That's worth last place in the tougher AFC North. It's a desperation game for the Ravens. Can they come up with a plan to move the football? Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Jaguars RB Bhayshul Tuten will rush for 100-plus yards The Ravens have a fairly solid run defense. But there's a caveat to this prediction. The Jaguars won't need a lot of points to win this game. The Ravens will struggle to put points on the board as the Jaguars stack the box against Derrick Henry. That means the Jaguars will be content to pound the ground game once they get a double-digit lead. And that means more carries for Tuten. He's coming off a 104-yard rushing performance against the Colts. And he should hit the mark again. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said he liked what he saw from Tuten, according to jacksonville.com. "I thought Tuten played really well (against the Colts)," Coen said. "He was seeing it. I thought he was a little more patient in this game. He was running through contact. He was explosive in the passing game. Tuten had a great week of practice, and it really carried over." Tuten said things fell into place , according to ESPN. "We knew it was going to rain," Tuten said. "We knew we were going to run the ball, and we just went out and imposed our will." Things are set up nicely for Tuten to have another big game. Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence will throw three TD passes Even if Tuten runs up and down the field, the Ravens will commit to stopping him inside the 10-yard line. That will open up opportunities for Lawrence to complete drives with TD passes. This season, Lawrence has 17 touchdown passes with four interceptions. And Lawrence is trying to keep the Jaguars in all-business mode , according to news4jax.com. "Winning your division is really important, but I think for us, it's really just going week by week," Lawrence said. "It's not something we think, 'Oh, we're a few games up. We're in a good spot. We can relax.' That's not really at all how we think. We got a lot of football left." The Ravens have two choices on defense. They can take chances and try to create splash plays. Or they can sit back and try to keep the game close, where they could steal one in the fourth quarter. If they take chances against Lawrence, he will simply hit them with longer strikes. It seems like a no-win situation for the Ravens. And a big day for Lawrence and the Jaguars. Ravens RB Derrick Henry will set season high in carries Make no doubt about it. The Ravens are going to put a saddle on Henry and try to ride him to a victory. Henry has 24 carries twice this year. But his season high of 26 came against the Cowboys in overtime. Look for him to eclipse that number. That is, if the Ravens can keep the ball long enough for him to rack up carries while the game is still within reach. But it's possible the Ravens will feed Henry even if they fall behind by two scores. That's all because the only real path to a win is through Henry. Henry has been the recent subject of trade rumors because of the injury to Jackson. The Giants have been in that conversation, but head coach John Harbaugh said it's hard to make big trades , according to Giants.com. "We're going to do the most we can possibly do to try to get some things done," Harbaugh said. "It's hard to get deals done. It's hard. You can see how hard it is, but we're going to do our best and what's for our team. And the best thing we can do, the main thing we're going to do is focus on our guys and get ready to play the game. But all that other stuff is definitely going on behind the scenes at all times." For now, Henry remains with the Ravens. And he has to be their leader on Thursday night. picks.blurb: QB NONE: Lamar Jackson? Out. Tyler Huntley? Likely out. Joe Fagnano? Also bitten by the injury bug. In other words, if you are within driving distance of M&T Bank Stadium on Thursday night - watch out and check the caller ID. You may be asked to play quarterback for the Ravens. As far as quarterbacks with experience go, Baltimore signed Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis. Jesse Minter might have to spin the QB wheel and hope for the best. On the road again: In Week 8, the Jaguars played a real home game at EverBank Stadium for the first time since Sept. 27. They had enough time to do some laundry, make sure nothing was out of place and maybe sleep in their own bed for a night or two before packing those bags once again. That Week 8 contest was the only true home game for Jacksonville during an eight-week stretch. The Jags' next home game isn't until Nov. 29 (Week 12) against the Titans. That's a lot of luggage. Show us what you've got, Brian Thomas Jr.: It's the last game before the NFL trade deadline for both teams and perhaps no player is more intriguing than the 2024 first-round pick. Thomas is one player that didn't benefit from Liam Coen's arrival in Jacksonville, falling down the receiver depth chart. He was benched against the Texans in London and hauled in a touchdown against the Colts . His time with the Jags appears to be coming to an end, so will the team give him some extra reps to squeeze some more value out of the trade market? Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve, Tyler Huntley is dealing with a toe injury and last week's emergency option Joe Fagnano isn't healthy either. Good luck preparing for Thursday night under those circumstances. Jacksonville has injury issues of its own, including season-ending losses for DaVon Hamilton and Eric Murray, which should give Derrick Henry a fighting chance to keep this competitive. But Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars have far more ways to win. I expect the Ravens to lean heavily on Henry, shorten the game and eventually run out of answers once the Jaguars build a lead. The visitors should win this one comfortably. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Jaguars 30, Ravens 6 With Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both hurt and Derrick Henry sputtering, the Ravens approach midseason essentially rudderless. Getting a short week to prepare for a top cotender under these circumstances seems like a disaster. Baltimore's only hope is a full-on unraveling by Jacksonville, but Trevor Lawrence should be able to take whatever he's given to comfortably direct an easy win and potenial blowout. However, the law firm of Fagnano, Reed and Slovis won't be as fortunate. Jacksonville wins big in B-More. away.blurb: The Jaguars posted their final injury report against the Ravens. Antonio Johnson is good to go, even though he was a limited participant in practice this season. Then again, easing him back into action was probably the best course of action, so he's back at full strength, or as close to it, on Sunday Night Football. While Johnson is good to go, defensive end Travon Walker (rib) and running back Bhaysul Tuten are listed as questionable. Head coach Liam Coen stated that Tuten will be a game-time decision . Offensive guard Ezra Cleveland was limited in practice due to knee and ankle injuries, but Coen says he'll suit up against the Ravens. Linebacker Branson Combs (shoulder), cornerback Jarrian Jones (ankle), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring), and running back Chris Rodriguez also practiced on a limited basis but were cleared to play. With Johnson back in the fold, defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile will be able to get creative in an effort to overwhelm 2026 third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano, who'll get the starting nod with Lamar Johnson and Tyler Huntley out for the season. Aside from Johnson, Jacksonville also has Kaevon Merriweather and Rayuan Lane III at safety. The Jacksonville Jaguars will face off against the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night. Although there's a chance running back Bhayshul Tuten won't suit up for the game, the Jags will get reinforcements on defense . Antonio Johnson will be back after missing the win over the Indianapolis Colts due to an ankle injury. Having him back will be huge since Jacksonville lost fellow safety Eric Murray and defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the rest of the year. Antonio Johnson didn't appear in the Jaguars' final injury report vs. the Ravens It's worth noting that Davon Hamilton and Eric Murray also popped up on the injury report, but both of them are landed on the injured reserve list after season-ending injuries in the win over the Colts. Meanwhile, Lane was just named Defensive Player of the Week after registering three passes defensed and returning an interception for a touchdown after picking up Daniel Jones. Report: Jaguars Trade Urgency ‘Amplified' After Injury Unlock the latest Heavy on Jaguars news — direct to your inbox. The Jacksonville Jaguars are expected to be without defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the rest of the 2026 season due to a torn quad. With the trade deadline approaching, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN noted that the Jaguars' need for a defensive tackle has been amplified due to the injury. He also reported that the belief in league circles was that the team would explore upgrades on the line before the injury. Jacksonville Jaguars Ramping Up Search for Defensive Line Help John Shipley of Jaguars OnSI noted that the Jaguars needed to improve their pass rush, and that could have been in the form of a defensive lineman prior to the game. “Simply put, if the Jaguars struggle to impact Jones with their pass-rush on Sunday, then they will have to raise the urgency to add a pass-rusher at the deadline,” wrote Shipley on the Jaguars' need prior to Week 8. “Regardless of whether it is edge help or interior defensive line reinforcements, this game and matchup should tell the Jaguars how badly they need to add some help.” The issue now is that Hamilton was their best run-defending threat. They went from needing a pass-rushing interior lineman to a player who can impact the game in both the pass and run. So, they will either need to take a bigger swing or look to take multiple swings on the line. Shipley acknowledged the difference after the game. “Jacksonville was likely already in the market for a pocket-pushing three-technique who could make an impact on passing downs next to Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, Arik Armstead, and Ruke Orhorhoro,” he added. “That is still a need, too. But now so is nose tackle.” Shipley adds that Roy Lopez of the Arizona Cardinals, Vita Vea and A'Shawn Robinson of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and Moro Ojomo of the Philadelphia Eagles are the names to watch for. Jaguars Might Be Without Hamilton After 2026 The big question for Hamilton is whether he will be with the team after this season. Hamilton will be entering free agency after the year. The interior lineman has been with Jacksonville for seven years, but will be 30 years old this upcoming season. So, the Jags could let him test the market and try to get younger on the line. away.blurb: Sources: tests revealed that Ravens’ QB Tyler “Snoop” Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury. Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is out indefinitely with a thumb injury, Huntley’s season is over due to turf toe, and QB Joe Fagnano will start Thursday night vs. Jacksonville. pic.twitter.com/Cok4gbSvH3 Baltimore was favored in the lookahead line for this game before Week 8 with Jackson back in action, but the two-time league MVP was injured on the first offensive play for Baltimore and has since been ruled out for the next four weeks as he's set to go on injured reserve. So, the line re-opened with Jacksonville as a 7.5-point favorite on Sunday night. Now, that line has moved 2.5 more points with Huntley out and Fagnano (ankle) set to start. DraftKings Sportsbook has the Jaguars set as 10-point road favorites as they look to move to 6-2 this season. The Jaguars are very capable of blowing out bad teams, as they took down the Indianapolis Colts -- 42-7 -- in Week 8. The Ravens (4-4) are major long shots to make the playoffs in the AFC, and there's a chance Jackson could end up missing the rest of the season if Baltimore is out of the mix by the time he's ready to return. Jaguars vs. Ravens Odds Continue to Shift Towards Jacksonville With Joe Fagnano Set to Start in NFL Week 9 Skip to main content ON SI Things keep getting worse for the Baltimore Ravens at quarterback, as they've lost Lamar Jackson to a thumb injury and Tyler Huntley (turf toe) is done for the season. That has put third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano in line to start in Week 9 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, which has caused a massive move in the odds. Fagnano played a lot of Sunday's loss against the Buffalo Bills, completing 10 of his 21 pass attempts for 91 yards and a pick. He also had three carries for three yards and a fumble. The former UConn star is going to be in a tough spot against a Jacksonville team that is in the top-10 in the league in EPA/Play and success rate on defense while sporting the No. 1 run defense in the NFL. Bettors that were able to grab the Jags early in the week certainly have to be happy, as it seems like this game is going to close with Trevor Lawrence and Co. favored by 10 or more points. away.headline: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Injury Could Mean Larger Role For 1 Veteran
away.blurb: Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten did not practice Tuesday as the result of an ankle/foot injury. Tuten was also listed as a non-participant in the walkthrough on the practice field Monday, with that day's injury report being just an estimate. Rodriguez himself was limited in Tuesday's practice with a hand injury, but that doesn't take away from the fact that he would be the expected bell cow of the offense if Tuten can't play. Tuten has played a massive role in the offense through the first seven games, getting more carries than Rodriguez in every game but one (Week 6). Rodriguez has 45 carries for 209 yards (4.6 yards per carry) and three touchdowns this season, scoring two rushing touchdowns from 20+ yards out. This included a 28-yard touchdown in Week 8 against the Indianapolis Colts, with Rodriguez and Tuten each taking a step forward in giving the Jaguars the explosive rushing game they have been looking for. “It's there. I mean, just watch the film, like, it's there. There's been plenty of times where me and Bhayshul [Tuten] have talked, and we're like, man, if we just slowed down a little bit or had a bit more patience, or if we would have read it out all the way through the guy and not just reading our first read, but our second read, man, we'll have so many explosives," Rodriguez said about the explosive runs during the bye week. "And we talked about it today. There are so many yards that we left out there in this past game. It's over, we can't get them back, but the only thing we can do is learn from it and move on.” The rest of the Jaguars injury report for Tuesday had the following players listed as limited: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Injury Could Mean Larger Role For 1 Veteran Skip to main content SI.COM JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have quite the lengthy injury report ahead of their Thursday Night Football matchup with the Baltimore Ravens, but there is one name that jumps off the page. home.headline: Final injury report: Antonio Johnson gives Jaguars a spark Ravens aren't ready for
home.blurb: The Jaguars posted their final injury report against the Ravens. Antonio Johnson is good to go, even though he was a limited participant in practice this season. Then again, easing him back into action was probably the best course of action, so he's back at full strength, or as close to it, on Sunday Night Football. While Johnson is good to go, defensive end Travon Walker (rib) and running back Bhaysul Tuten are listed as questionable. Head coach Liam Coen stated that Tuten will be a game-time decision . Offensive guard Ezra Cleveland was limited in practice due to knee and ankle injuries, but Coen says he'll suit up against the Ravens. Linebacker Branson Combs (shoulder), cornerback Jarrian Jones (ankle), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring), and running back Chris Rodriguez also practiced on a limited basis but were cleared to play. With Johnson back in the fold, defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile will be able to get creative in an effort to overwhelm 2026 third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano, who'll get the starting nod with Lamar Johnson and Tyler Huntley out for the season. Aside from Johnson, Jacksonville also has Kaevon Merriweather and Rayuan Lane III at safety. The Jacksonville Jaguars will face off against the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night. Although there's a chance running back Bhayshul Tuten won't suit up for the game, the Jags will get reinforcements on defense . Antonio Johnson will be back after missing the win over the Indianapolis Colts due to an ankle injury. Having him back will be huge since Jacksonville lost fellow safety Eric Murray and defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the rest of the year. Antonio Johnson didn't appear in the Jaguars' final injury report vs. the Ravens It's worth noting that Davon Hamilton and Eric Murray also popped up on the injury report, but both of them are landed on the injured reserve list after season-ending injuries in the win over the Colts. Meanwhile, Lane was just named Defensive Player of the Week after registering three passes defensed and returning an interception for a touchdown after picking up Daniel Jones. home.headline: Ravens to trade for Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals to fill QB void: Report
home.blurb: Ravens to trade for QB Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals: Report – NBC New York Skip to content Breaking Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to potential season-ending injuries last week. By Logan Reardon • Published 16 minutes ago • Updated 16 minutes ago Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. There's a new quarterback in Baltimore. Days after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley suffered potential season-ending injuries , the Ravens reportedly traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the news on Wednesday, adding that the trade is expected to be finalized over the weekend. Watch NBC 4 free wherever you are With the Ravens playing on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the earliest that Brissett could make his debut for the team would be on Monday, Nov. 16, against the Los Angeles Chargers . Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start for Baltimore against Jacksonville, with inexperienced quarterbacks Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis serving as the backups. Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and two turnovers in his relief debut Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after Jackson and Huntley went down. The two-time MVP Jackson, coming off three missed games with an ankle injury, suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery on his first throw last Sunday. His backup, Huntley, returned to the field, but he went down with a turf toe injury that will require surgery in the second quarter. Brissett, 33, lost his starting job to Gardner Minshew on Sunday. That made him an obvious trade candidate before next Tuesday's deadline, and the Ravens pounced quickly. Brissett started Arizona's first eight games this season and went 3-5 with 1,719 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Detroit Lions star Jack Campbell says he has ‘full movement' of lower body after scary on-field injury Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol as Shedeur Sanders could start for Browns An 11-year NFL veteran, Brissett has several ties to the Ravens' coaching staff. Quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork held the same position for the Cardinals last season and passing game coordinator Marcus Brady was a Colts assistant when Brissett was there from 2018-20. Brissett was drafted in 2016 by the New England Patriots and has gone on to play for six teams before Baltimore -- the Patriots (2016, 2024), Indianapolis Colts (2017-20), Miami Dolphins (2021), Cleveland Browns (2022), Washington Commanders (2023) and Cardinals (2025-26). home.blurb: In the same report, Dan Graziano noted the Ravens will "work to solve the problem" with Jackson out for the time being and are "open to a number of ideas" at the quarterback spot with Jacoby Brissett cited as someone they could "look into" acquiring. Bagent immediately stood out as a potential trade option for Baltimore because Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle came from the Chicago Bears where the two worked together last season. Few teams are harder to figure out right now than the Colts, even though they have acknowledged their need to sell by trading away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Jones' availability might be even harder to figure out because head coach Shane Steichen told reporters on Monday he will remain the starting quarterback. Of the potential quarterback options mentioned by Fowler and Graziano, Brissett might be the most available. He was benched by the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in favor of Gardner Minshew II, who led the offense to 23 points in the fourth quarter and overtime in a 33-30 victory over the Dallas Cowboys. There's no good situation for the Ravens right now because Tyler Huntley also suffered a turf toe injury that is expected to keep him out for the remainder of the season. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano is set to make his first career start on Thursday night against the Jaguars. It has not been determined if Jackson will miss the rest of the season, but an IR stint will keep him out for at least the next four weeks. The schedule does help them because they have a bye in Week 13, meaning Jackson could theoretically be back on Dec. 13 with five games remaining. Amid uncertainty about Lamar Jackson's status for the remainder of the 2026 season, the Baltimore Ravens are seeking help at quarterback prior to the trade deadline as they try to stay in the AFC playoff race. Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , some of the options the Ravens are looking at include Daniel Jones and Tyson Bagent. Jackson returned on Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after missing three games then injured his thumb on his first pass attempt. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters after the 36-10 loss to Buffalo that Jackson would undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve. The Bears may not be eager to trade Bagent since Caleb Williams has already missed time this season, though they did get one quality start from Case Keenum during Williams' absence that might make head coach Ben Johnson comfortable if he had to step in. The Colts are reportedly open to trading Jonathan Taylor, but they still played him 38 offensive snaps and risked a potential injury in Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur announced Minshew will remain the starter going forward and rookie Carson Beck will be the No. 2, leaving Brissett as the emergency third quarterback. home.headline: Ravens injury report: Nate Wiggins is questionable, Vega Ioane to play
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens could be without one of their most important defensive players Thursday night, as starting cornerback Nate Wiggins is questionable for their Week 9 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars . Baltimore released its final injury report Wednesday, listing Wiggins as questionable because of a stinger and illness. The second-year cornerback did not practice Wednesday after participating fully during Monday's and Tuesday's sessions, creating uncertainty about his availability against Trevor Lawrence and Jacksonville's passing attack. His availability matters because Jacksonville has multiple receiving threats capable of challenging Baltimore's secondary. The Ravens will already be without safety Jaylinn Hawkins, who has been ruled out because of a knee injury after missing all three practices. If Wiggins cannot play, Baltimore may need more from its remaining cornerbacks, including T.J. Tampa, as defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver adjusts coverage assignments. Vega Ioane cleared to return against Jacksonville The rookie first-round pick missed the Buffalo game after suffering an MCL sprain, creating another challenge for a Ravens offensive line that has dealt with multiple injuries. Ioane was limited Monday before participating fully in the final two practices, putting him in position to return to his starting right guard role. His expected availability comes at an important time for Baltimore, which will start undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano against Jacksonville. Fagnano has also cleared the injury report after dealing with an ankle injury suffered against Buffalo. The Ravens need improved protection and a productive running game to help their inexperienced quarterback, making Ioane's potential return particularly valuable. Ravens rule out three players, list Adam Randall questionable Baltimore has ruled out quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley, along with Hawkins. Jackson is dealing with a right thumb injury that requires surgery, while Huntley's season is over because of a turf toe injury. Running back Adam Randall is questionable because of a neck injury. Randall has been designated to return from injured reserve and participated fully throughout the week, but he must be activated before he can play. The Ravens enter Thursday's game at 4-4 after three straight losses, making Wiggins's availability and Ioane's expected return significant developments ahead of an important AFC matchup. Ioane participated fully in Tuesday's and Wednesday's practices and does not carry an injury designation into Thursday's game. The Cincinnati Bengals needed a spectacular performance from Joe Burrow to escape with an overtime victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, but oddsmakers aren’t expecting the same kind of offensive fireworks when Cincinnati faces the Atlanta Falcons next weekend. Still, with the Bengals’ defense continuing to struggle, the early betting lines suggest another potentially high-scoring affair. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , Cincinnati opened as a 3.5-point favorite over Atlanta, with the Bengals listed at -225 on the moneyline and the Falcons at +188. The opening over/under was set at 49.5 points. The latest FanDuel odds show Cincinnati remaining a 3.5-point favorite, although the price has shifted to -102 for the Bengals and -120 for the Falcons. The Bengals’ moneyline has moved to -184, while Atlanta’s stands at +154. The over/under has increased by one point to 50.5. The Bengals enter the matchup following a wild 43-36 overtime victory over Tennessee that featured five touchdown passes and three interceptions from Burrow, who ultimately delivered the winning score by scrambling nine yards around left end for just the second offensive overtime touchdown in franchise history. But while Cincinnati’s offense once again demonstrated its ability to put points on the scoreboard, the defense raised serious questions. The Bengals surrendered 36 points in regulation to a Tennessee team that entered Sunday’s game with just one victory, delivering a performance that looked disturbingly similar to the defensive struggles that plagued Cincinnati throughout last season. Atlanta, meanwhile, is coming off a 16-0 shutout loss to a Tampa Bay Buccaneers squad that did not complete a single pass. That sets up an intriguing matchup between a Falcons offense that couldn’t find the end zone and a Bengals defense that had difficulty keeping the Titans out of it. The Cincinnati Bengals didn't practice Wednesday after flying to Madrid ahead of their NFL Week 9 game against the Atlanta Falcons . The team's injury report , an estimation of practice participation, includes several defensive players. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. Turner was injured during the fourth quarter of the team's NFL Week 8 overtime win against the Tennessee Titans at Paycor Stadium. Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said Nov. 2 that Turner and Johnson are day-to-day. Cincinnati will be without rookie Cashius Howell , who was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week. away.headline: Bengals Injury Report: Ja'Marr Chase's Status Upgraded on Thursday as Bengals Continue Titans Preparation
away.blurb: Kyle Dugger (quad) continues to not practice as he heads toward another missed game this week. Fellow safety Jordan Battle was also limited again with a shoulder injury, but he's been playing through that issue in outings over the last few weeks. On the Titans' side of things, starting defensive tackle John Franklin-Meyers (groin) upgraded to limited and starting receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice for a second-straight day. Bengals Injury Report: Ja'Marr Chase's Status Upgraded on Thursday as Bengals Continue Titans Preparation Skip to main content SI.COM The Bengals dropped their Thursday injury report ahead of the Titans game, and Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) got upgraded to full status on the report after not practicing due to that small issue and rest in general on Wednesday. He told the media on Thursday his ankle feels fine. Cincinnati is pretty clean besides those names. Cincinnati head coach Zac Taylor has had to shuffle around his tight end room due to all of the injuries in recent weeks. Erick All just went on season-ending injured reserve with a torn ACL, and fellow tight end Tanner Hudson tore a pec this season as well. "Attention to detail has been really important to him," Taylor said about rookie tight end Jack Endries as he gets primed for more snaps. "Waiting for his moment, you can tell he never knew when his number was going to be called. He's really got to know three different positions and so I've got trust, just watching him operate in practice and in meetings and in training camp, that if needed, he was going to be ready to go, and there was a time where he wasn't needed because we had everybody healthy, and now's that time. So I'm not nervous at all about using him. I think he's earning the opportunity. I'm excited to watch him play." Taylor also echoed confidence in backup safety PJ Jules, who is filling in for Dugger's reserve role. "PJ brings a lot of energy. It's really important to him," Taylor noted. "He's done a great job on special teams in his roles. He stepped into safety. So when we need to continue to rely on depth at the safety position, I feel very confident in PJ and Russ (Yeast)." home.blurb: "Asked about Pearce, Stefanski said the Falcons are pleased with where he is in terms of being football ready," wrote team reporter Tori McElhaney . "He's been working out with the Falcons strength staff for the last month, per his suspension rules. That said, Stefanski added the Falcons will use the rest of this week to determine how many snaps Pearce gets this Sunday against the Cincinnati Bengals." Wide receiver Zachariah Branch sat out as expected with a hamstring injury. Stefanski has already ruled the rookie return man out for Sunday's game. Branch was the only player to log a "DNP" on Wednesday, though. Linebacker Divine Deablo, running back Brian Robinson Jr. and LB Yasir Abdullah (designated to return from IR) were limited participants to begin Week 9. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. was a full participant. Check out the Falcons' full estimated Wednesday injury report below, and come back for updates from Cincinnati's practice report this afternoon. WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring): DNP/OUT The Atlanta Falcons have arrived in Madrid, Spain for their Week 9 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals . The team held a brief walkthrough on Wednesday morning and released a simulated injury report shortly after. Edge rusher James Pearce Jr. was listed as a full participant for the first time all season. Pearce, who was suspended for the first eight games for his violation of the NFL's personal conduct policy, is expected to make his 2026 debut this Sunday against the Bengals. The Defensive Rookie of the Year finalist led all rookies in sacks with 10.5 last season. Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said Pearce was in good shape and that the team would monitor him this week to determine how much the second-year edge rusher would play against Cincinnati. home.headline: Is Baker Mayfield Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Falcons vs. Buccaneers in NFL Week 8)
home.blurb: Is Baker Mayfield Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Falcons vs. Buccaneers in NFL Week 8) Skip to main content ON SI Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield returned from a three-game absence due to a dislocated thumb in Week 7, and he's off the team's injury report and expected to play in Week 8. Mayfield guided the Bucs to their second win of the season against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, and oddsmakers are buying the Buccaneers at home in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons. The Buccaneers are favored to win their matchup with the Falcons, sitting as 2.5-point favorites in the odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . After a 1-5 start to the season, Tampa Bay's win over Carolina thrust it back into the mix to win the division this season. Another win over an NFC South opponent would go a long way for Tampa Bay getting into the playoffs, and the running game has really stepped forward in recent weeks with both Mayfield and Jalon Daniels under center. Mayfield wasn't asked to do much against Carolina, completing just seven of his 11 passes for 76 yards and a score. He's completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 679 yards, three scores and two picks in four games. Daniels led Tampa Bay to one win while Mayfield was sidelined, but it's pretty clear that oddsmakers view the former No. 1 overall pick as a major upgrade under center. Mayfield and the Bucs take on Altanta and Chicago over the next two weeks before their bye. Atlanta is currently one game ahead of Tampa Bay in the NFC South, but a win on Sunday would vault the Bucs into second in the divison, just a half-game back of the Panthers (3-4). home.headline: Cowboys vs. Colts prediction: Odds, expert picks, QB matchup, injury update, betting trends, and stats
home.blurb: Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. home.headline: Dallas Cowboys injury tracker ahead of Week 9 vs. Colts includes both first-round rookies, and one hopeful sign for the defense
home.blurb: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer provided a bunch of updates Wednesday before the team's first practice of the week. He touched on linebacker Dee Winters, tight end Jake Ferguson, safety Caleb Downs, and several others. The official injury report comes out later in the day, but these are the updates Schottenheimer brought up for now. Winters is doing individual work after suffering an injury in Week 6 against the Green Bay Packers. His return would give Dallas additional depth at linebacker, which it desperately needs. The intriguing part is how the Cowboys deploy him. Since Winters went down, the plan has been to play Shemar James as the green dot defender with a rotation of DeMarvion Overshown and Jaishawn Barham alongside him. Before Overshown's return, however, Winters was the weakside linebacker while Barham operated as the green dot. Dallas does have options if push comes to shove. On the 53-man roster, Markquese Bell and Alijah Clark could step up. On the practice squad, Reddy Steward played some safety in the preseason, but he's out of practice squad elevations. Perhaps the worst news of all involves Jalen Thompson. The safety remains on injured reserve, and his 21-day practice window hasn't been opened. A return seemingly isn't near. Malachi Lawrence's injury thins out the edge rushers All told, it's mostly negative news for the Cowboys on the injury front. And against the Colts, a banged-up secondary could be very costly as the Cowboys are running out of time to get a win streak going. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The New York Jets head to Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, November 8, trying to keep their season from slipping further away against a Kansas City Chiefs team that is looking to halt a skid of its own. The Jets have lost three straight. They are 2-6 overall (1-3 on the road) and approaching the cellar in the AFC East. The Chiefs are 3-0 at home and 5-2 overall but have lost two in a row and sit in second in the AFC West a ½ game behind the Broncos. The Jets are coming off a frustrating 38-33 home loss to the Raiders in which they produced plenty of offense but couldn’t stop Vegas late. New York scored on its first six possessions, led 23-14 at halftime and 30-21 during the third quarter, but Las Vegas rallied with back-to-back touchdown drives to take a lead late. Geno Smith threw for 290 yards, two touchdowns and an interception, while Braelon Allen rushed for a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown and Adonai Mitchell produced a career-best 142 receiving yards with a score. A big red flag for the Jets continues to be their inefficiency in the red zone on offense and defense: New York went just 2-for-6 in the red zone while Las Vegas finished 4-for-4. Kansas City also melted late in their game last Sunday against the Broncos, blowing a 24-13 fourth-quarter lead in a 28-24 loss at Denver. Patrick Mahomes played much better than he had in the Chiefs’ previous defeat at Seattle, completing 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, including a 73-yard touchdown to Emmett Johnson . Denver, however, scored 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter, Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal, and after Mahomes drove the Chiefs inside the Broncos’ 5 in the final minute, Denver made a goal-line stand capped by Malcolm Roach’s sack on fourth down. Historically, the matchup has produced some memorable games. The most recent meeting was a few years ago on October 1, 2023, when Kansas City escaped MetLife Stadium with a 23-20 win. The Chiefs raced ahead 17-0 in the first quarter before the Jets rallied to tie the game at 20 behind Zach Wilson , who completed 28 of 39 passes for 245 yards and two touchdowns. Mahomes had an unusually uneven passing night, finishing 18 of 30 for 203 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, but Kansas City retook the lead on Butker’s 26-yard field goal and Mahomes used his legs to help drain the clock late. That game offers a useful blueprint for Sunday’s upset-minded Jets: withstand Kansas City’s early punch, keep Mahomes from creating explosives and turn offensive production into touchdowns rather than field goals. For the Chiefs, the larger storyline is whether they can rediscover their finishing touch after consecutive losses on the road. away.blurb: Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid announced on Wednesday morning that rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods , the Chiefs' first-round draft pick this year, would sit out practice with a neck stinger Wednesday, clouding his status for Sunday's Jets game. The injury traces to Kansas City's Week 8 game against the Denver Broncos . Woods exited in the first half after getting caught up in blocks on a screen play, and the Chiefs ruled him out after he played only three defensive snaps. Neck problems also appeared on the injury report earlier this season, when Woods was limited ahead of the Week 6 game against the Los Angeles Chargers , according to RotoWire . Woods is a developing rotational piece, so his absence would mainly test Kansas City's interior depth. Jones and Tonga would absorb more snaps, with Omarr Norman-Lott , recently designated to return from the physically unable to perform list, another option. Adonai Mitchell had seven catches for a career-high 142 yards and a touchdown in his second game back after missing four with a finger injury that required surgery. If Wilson is out, Mitchell and rookie Omar Cooper Jr. — who was held without a target after consecutive 100-yard receiving games — likely would be counted on to pick up the slack in the passing game. home.headline: Chiefs injury report: Travis Kelce remains limited after ankle flare-up
home.blurb: The Chiefs will take on the New York Jets, hoping to avoid a third consecutive defeat when they return home on Sunday. However, Kelce’s availability is one of the situations the team will be monitoring. The Chiefs announced the latest update on Kelce after Wednesday’s practice, with the 11-time NFL Pro Bowler listed as a limited participant. The limited designation does not mean he is in danger of missing Sunday’s game. However, it is another indication that the issue he has been playing through remains a concern. Travis Kelce and the Kansas City Chiefs are coming off their second straight loss and will look to get back on track in Week 9. The Chiefs fell 28-24 to the Denver Broncos on Sunday after surrendering a late lead. Kelce was one of Patrick Mahomes’ top targets. He finished with five catches for 67 yards and remained involved in the offense despite appearing uncomfortable at times. Kelce has been playing through an ankle injury he sustained in Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers. The 37-year-old appeared to aggravate the injury during the loss to Denver. He was seen limping after a play in the second half, but managed to finish the game. Kansas City will keep a close eye on Kelce as the week progresses. The Chiefs sit second in the AFC West and will host a Jets team that has managed just two wins this season and lost three straight. Sunday’s game kicks off at 1 p.m. ET, with live coverage on CBS. home.headline: Chiefs Announce Concerning Pete Woods Injury News Before Jets Game
home.blurb: Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid announced on Wednesday morning that rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods , the Chiefs' first-round draft pick this year, would sit out practice with a neck stinger Wednesday, clouding his status for Sunday's Jets game. The injury traces to Kansas City's Week 8 game against the Denver Broncos . Woods exited in the first half after getting caught up in blocks on a screen play, and the Chiefs ruled him out after he played only three defensive snaps. Neck problems also appeared on the injury report earlier this season, when Woods was limited ahead of the Week 6 game against the Los Angeles Chargers , according to RotoWire . Woods is a developing rotational piece, so his absence would mainly test Kansas City's interior depth. Jones and Tonga would absorb more snaps, with Omarr Norman-Lott , recently designated to return from the physically unable to perform list, another option. home.headline: Chiefs dealt double injury blow before facing Broncos
home.blurb: The Chiefs won the first meeting between the two teams in Week 1, demolishing the Broncos 31-10. But Denver has responded well since then, and now has the opportunity to move ahead of their division rivals in the standings. With the Broncos’ defense allowing just 18.3 points per game since Week 2, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense will have their work cut out for them. Unfortunately, Kansas City’s defense now won’t have two of their best players. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been downgraded to out with a shoulder injury after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report, while veteran corner L’Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Sneed will miss at least the next four games, leaving the Chiefs without two important members of their secondary against Denver. Sneed is also dealing with a recurring injury, with the knee issue forcing him to be limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. But his being placed on IR clearly signals the injury is more serious than anticipated, with Week 12 viewed as his expected return date. In six appearances this season, Sneed has recorded 32 combined tackles (22 solo), three pass breakups, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery. The Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos will meet for an important AFC West showdown on Sunday, with the division lead on the line. Kansas City enters at 5-1 after suffering their first loss of the NFL season in Seattle last weekend, while Denver is 5-2 and riding a three-game winning streak after beating the Cardinals in Arizona. After returning to the lineup in Week 3, he suffered another setback during Wednesday’s practice ahead of the rematch with Denver. In five games this season, Delane has recorded 27 combined tackles (17 solo), three tackles for loss, five pass breakups, and one interception. He’s also played nearly every defensive snap since returning in Week 3. The NFC North is crowded with the Lions sitting third despite having but two losses. Miami is in the cellar in the AFC East. Lets get the obvious out of the way. The difference between these teams is substantial: Detroit is averaging 29.0 points and an NFL-best 395.4 yards per game, while Miami is averaging only 16.7 points and 290.0 yards. Detroit’s latest victory was arguably its most impressive of the season, a 19-15 win over the previously unbeaten Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field last Sunday. The Lions trailed 7-6 at halftime before Jahmyr Gibbs broke loose for a 30-yard touchdown in the third quarter. Minnesota regained the lead at 15-12 with 8:44 remaining, but Jared Goff responded by directing a seven-play, 69-yard drive and finding Jameson Williams for the go-ahead seven-yard touchdown with 4:35 left. Goff finished 18-of-25 for 176 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Gibbs carried 23 times for 153 yards and a touchdown and Williams caught four passes for 70 yards including the decisive score. The victory came at a cost, however, as linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a neck injury and was listed as doubtful on the early Week 9 injury information. The Dolphins are coming off a game that typified their frustrating season, blowing a 13-3 halftime lead in a 24-19 loss to the New England Patriots. Malik Willis and the Miami offense were in control early, but New England erupted for 21 unanswered second-half points, including touchdown passes of 43 and 48 yards from Drake Maye , to turn the game around. Miami finally answered when Willis connected with rookie Kevin Coleman Jr. for a 35-yard touchdown with 2:04 remaining, but the Dolphins failed on the ensuing two-point conversion and New England recovered the onside kick. Willis finished 21-of-32 for 211 yards, two touchdowns and an interception but was sacked five times, while Miami managed only 269 total yards and 74 on the ground. Although the Lions and Dolphins meet infrequently, their most recent games have been surprisingly competitive. Miami leads the all-time regular-season series 8-5, but Detroit won three straight meetings from 2010 through 2018 before Miami answered with a 31-27 victory at Ford Field in 2022. That most recent meeting was an offensive showcase: Tua Tagovailoa threw for 382 yards and three touchdowns, Tyreek Hill piled up 188 receiving yards and the Dolphins rallied from a 27-17 deficit to win, despite Goff throwing for 321 yards. The Detroit Lions (5-2) will travel to Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6) in Week 9, in a battle between teams at two very different stages of their roster development. While the Lions are shaking off some early-season mistakes, they’ve strung together three wins, including back-to-back wins in their division, while the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild under their latest regime. The folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7 points . The Dolphins made a general manager and head coaching change this offseason, firing GM Chris Grier and coach Mike McDaniel after four unsuccessful seasons and hiring Jon-Eric Sullivan as their new GM and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley as their new coach. Like most new regimes, the new staff got to work early, cutting veteran contracts, including quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. They also traded away former first-round pick Jaylen Waddle for a trio of picks to use in the 2026 NFL Draft to help them with the rebuild. Step one in establishing a new foundation was signing Malik Willis as their new signal caller—who most recently played in Green Bay with Hafley—and drafting six (!) rookie starters, including first-round picks guard Kadyn Proctor and corner Chris Johnson, as well as second-round pick linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, third-round receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe. They also have another eight rookies on their 53-man roster, meaning over 25% of the Dolphins roster (14 players) is made up of first-year players. As you would expect with a young roster at the beginning of a rebuild, the Dolphins have struggled out of the gate. In Week 1, the Raiders beat them by two touchdowns; the 49ers won by three touchdowns the week after; and the Chiefs beat them by two touchdowns in Week 3. In Week 4, they showed signs of improvement, losing to the Vikings by only five points; the Bengals won by just seven in Week 5, and in Week 6, they got their first win of the season, beating the Jets by three points. On Sunday, the Dolphins and Patriots squared off in an AFC East showdown, and while the Dolphins built a 13-3 lead at the half, the Patriots scored 21 unanswered points to go up 24-13 late in the fourth quarter. Willis connected on an explosive touchdown pass at the 2-minute warning to bring them close, but a failed 2-point conversion and a failed onside kick set the final score at 24-19. After splitting their first four games, the Lions have found their footing with three straight wins. Detroit hung 45 points on the Cardinals in Arizona, edged the Packers 20-17 coming out of its bye, and then handed Minnesota its first loss of the season at Ford Field. The Lions are a pristine 4-0 at home but just 1-2 on the road, and this is their first road game since that Week 5 win in Arizona. Meanwhile, the Dolphins opened the Jeff Hafley era 0-5 before finally breaking through with a 28-25 win over the Jets in Week 7. They couldn't build on it, falling 24-19 at home to the New England Patriots last week, and Miami is now 0-3 at Hard Rock Stadium this season. Say what you want about the Dolphins, but their last four games have been decided by a touchdown or less. Detroit Lions @ Miami Dolphins This season, Detroit has been one of the most explosive offences in football, averaging 29.0 points and 395.4 yards per game, and the over has hit in five of its seven contests. Jahmyr Gibbs entered Week 8 averaging 103.3 rushing yards per game as one of the early front-runners for NFL Offensive Player of the Year, and Jared Goff hadn't thrown an interception through six games before succumbing to the pressure of Minnesota's blitz-happy defence and tossing a pick. 2026/27 NFL - Awards AP Offensive Player of the Year The surprise has been the defence, which held Green Bay to 17 points and Minnesota to 15 in back-to-back weeks. Still, the Lions have been a tough team to back as a favourite, going 1-3-1 against the spread when laying points entering last week. As for the Dolphins, Malik Willis has given them some life with his legs, but the offence ranks near the bottom of the league at 16.7 points per game. Willis entered last week with just four touchdown passes against four interceptions, and Miami's defence has generated the fewest sacks in the NFL while allowing 25.9 points per game. That said, Willis has multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games, so perhaps he's showing some signs of life as a passer. With Detroit's offence facing a defence that can't get home, siding with the Lions on the road makes sense, though a touchdown is a lot to lay for a team that has struggled to cover as a favourite. The over is worth a look as well, given how often Lions games have cleared the number. NFL Player Odds and Props Jahmyr Gibbs OVER 100.5 rushing yards Gibbs has been the engine of this Lions offence, entering Week 8 averaging 103.3 rushing yards per game on one of the league's heaviest workloads. Miami's defence has struggled to get off the field all season, and if Detroit builds a lead, the Lions will lean on Gibbs to bleed the clock in the Florida heat. The one thing to monitor is the shoulder injury that kept him out of practice ahead of the Vikings game, but with the Lions very concentrated in the run game, Gibbs should have ample opportunity to get above the century mark against the Dolphins. Malik Willis OVER 29.5 rushing yards We went with this prop last week, and Willis tallied just two yards on the ground. That lack of output was an anomaly, and we're going back to the well this week. He is the key to any Dolphins upset, and Willis' legs are clearly his most dangerous weapon. Willis is at his best when he's moving, and he ran for over 100 yards and two touchdowns across his two games heading into last week. Miami's offence is built around designed runs, zone reads and scrambles, and that shouldn't change against a Lions defence that has been aggressive in coverage. If the Dolphins fall behind, Willis will be forced to create on his own, which usually means more yards with his legs. Goff has been efficient and careful with the ball, throwing for 303 yards and two touchdowns against Green Bay and keeping the turnovers to a minimum. Amon-Ra St. Brown set a new career high in receiving yards in that game, and with Gibbs carrying the ground game and Jameson Williams stretching the field, this offence has a weapon at every level. Sam LaPorta has been quieter of late, but he remains a reliable red zone option for Goff. Production for the Lions was muted against a tough Minnesota defence as Goff passed for just 176 yards, but Gibbs was the alpha here with 153 yards and a touchdown on the ground and Williams adding a touchdown on four grabs for 70 yards. The bigger story over the last two weeks has been the defence. After giving up 17 touchdowns through the first four games, the Lions have tightened up considerably, holding two NFC North rivals to 32 combined points. Facing a Dolphins offence averaging just 16.7 points per game, Detroit's defence has a chance to keep that momentum going. Running back Ollie Gordon II has been the most consistent piece of this offence, rushing for 339 yards and four touchdowns on 72 carries heading into last week, when he put up 69 yards as a running back that lacks any receiving profile. Still, the Dolphins will need him to keep Detroit's offence on the sideline. Willis found a connection with rookie Caleb Douglas in the win over the Jets, while Malik Washington and tight end Greg Dulcich gave Willis options underneath. The problem is consistency, as Miami has not been able to string together complete performances through the air. It's to be expected for such a young team that's trying to find an identity as well as players for the future who will be around long-term as they rebuild into a contender. Defensively, Zach Sieler anchors the interior, but the Dolphins simply can't pressure the quarterback, and that's a dangerous combination against a passer like Goff. If Miami can't make Detroit uncomfortable, its best hope is controlling the clock with Gordon and Willis and keeping this one close into the fourth quarter. away.headline: NFL-Lions report positive progress for linebacker Campbell after injury
away.blurb: "Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time," the team said in a statement. Nov 2 (Reuters) - Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital, the NFL team said on Monday, a day after he was carried off the field with a frightening injury during a game against the Minnesota Vikings. Campbell lay motionless on the ground after levelling a hit on Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter at Ford Field and was taken to hospital after medical staff removed him from the field. The Pro Bowl linebacker, a captain for the team this season, was drafted by the Lions in the first round three years ago and coach Dan Campbell described him as the consummate teammate. "You get voted captain, that says a ton," said coach Campbell. "He earned every bit of that. He's trustworthy, he's dependable, he'd give you the shirt off his back. He's just all heart, man, all effort." (Reporting by Amy Tennery in New YorkEditing by Christian Radnedge)

away.headline: Detroit Lions LB Jack Campbell: 'I have full movement in my lower body'
away.blurb: Campbell was the No. 18 overall pick by the Lions in 2023 out of Iowa. News Sports Autos Entertainment Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals LIONS Detroit Lions LB Jack Campbell: 'I have full movement in my lower body' Dave Birkett Christian Romo Detroit Free Press Updated Nov. 4, 2026, 3:24 p.m. ET Hear this story Injured linebacker Jack Campbell said in a statement released by the Detroit Lions on Wednesday, Nov. 4, that he has "full movement" in his lower body, is "continuing to make progress with movement" in his upper body and remains "very optimistic" about his recovery. "My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers and support we've received over the past few days," the statement read. "It means more to us than words can express." Campbell was injured making a tackle on tight end T.J. Hockenson on the first play of the fourth quarter of the Lions' win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 1. Campbell's head appeared to hit Hockenson's left hip on the play. He fell face-first to the ground after making the stop and was motionless on the turf as doctors loaded him onto a backboard and took him to a waiting ambulance by medical cart. The game was delayed for about 10 minutes, and Ford Field sat silent while players from both teams surrounded the scene on a knee in prayer. Campbell remains in the hospital, and he said in his statement he's "incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time." "I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body," the statement said. "I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better." The Lions rallied to beat the Vikings after Campbell's injury, getting a stop on a key fourth-and-5 play on the next snap. Minnesota scored on its next possession to take a 15-12 lead, before the Lions scored the game-winning touchdown. After the game, Dan Campbell led an emotional locker room in prayer, and players said the win was dedicated to Jack Campbell. “Just seeing something like that, him being down for so long, yeah, I think from that moment on we really – it was for 4-6, man,” defensive end Aidan Hutchinson said. “And again, we don’t really know the status, but we’re praying for him.” In his statement, Jack Campbell thanked Lions trainers for their quick response, the doctors in charge of his recovery at Henry Ford Hospital and fans for keeping him in their minds. "My faith in God has never been stronger," the statement said. "I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we'll get through this." at the Caesars Superdome brings together two teams in very different positions, as the Cleveland Browns (5-3) take the field against the New Orleans Saints (2-5). Cleveland is third in the AFC North but just one game behind the first place Steelers. New Orleans has lost four of their last five games and sit last in the NFC South, but they are also only a game out of first as they return from their bye. The Superdome, however, has not been kind to the Saints who are winless in four home games (0-4). Cleveland, however, is a respectable 2-3 on the road this season. Plenty of positives happening with the Browns this season, but last week’s performance is not one of them. The Steelers thumped Cleveland, 27-6, in Pittsburgh. Cleveland was held without a touchdown for the first time this year, lost two fumbles, rushed for only 34 yards and surrendered eight sacks, while the Steelers piled up 200 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Forced to throw for much of the afternoon, Deshaun Watson completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards without an interception and Harold Fannin Jr. caught 10 passes for 154 yards. New Orleans has not played in a couple weeks, but their last game was also a loss to the Steelers, 16-10, in Paris on Oct. 25. The Saints managed only 18 rushing yards and were shut out in the second half, but quarterback Tyler Shough produced an encouraging performance through the air, completing 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards, one touchdown and one interception. It was symptomatic of the season to date: the offense has no balance. Historically, Cleveland leads the all-time series 13-7, but New Orleans has won each of the last three meetings, including the most recent matchup at this same venue on November 17, 2024. That game was tied 14-14 entering the fourth quarter before the Saints exploded for 21 unanswered points to win 35-14. Taysom Hill was the difference-maker, rushing seven times for 138 yards and three touchdowns, including fourth-quarter scoring runs of 33 and 75 yards, while Derek Carr threw for 248 yards and two touchdowns. Jameis Winston threw for 395 yards and two scores for Cleveland, but the Browns failed to turn their yardage into enough points. Two years later, the central question is similar for both clubs: which offense can translate production into touchdowns? Cleveland needs to protect Watson and rediscover a ground game that disappeared in Pittsburgh, while New Orleans needs Shough, Kamara and an offense coming out of the bye to take advantage of a Browns defense that just surrendered 200 rushing yards. away.headline: Saints get Jordyn Tyson, Kelvin Banks Jr. back at practice Wednesday in Browns prep
away.blurb: The New Orleans Saints received some encouraging injury news Wednesday as wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. returned to practice ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Cleveland Browns. Both players still on injured reserve were listed as limited participants on the Saints' first injury report of the week, marking an important step toward potentially returning to the lineup. Tyson and Banks Jr. have entered 21-day practice windows associated with their potential activations for the 53-man roster. Tyson, the rookie first round pick who is working his way back from a hamstring injury, gives the Saints another potential weapon in the passing game. He has been sidelined since August 12, never appearing in a preseason game and yet to make his regular season debut. Banks also returned to the practice field ahead of schedule after missing the past six games. His potential return from an ankle injury that required surgery would provide a boost to an offensive line looking to improve its pass protection and establish consistency in a faltering running game. The Saints had several other players dealing with injuries Wednesday. Running back C.J. Donaldson (shoulder/concussion), cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (shin) and offensive tackles Kelvin Banks Jr. and Asim Richards (thumb) were limited participants. Safety Justin Reid returned to full participation after dealing with a concussion, while guard Cesar Ruiz (knee) and defensive tackle Nathan Shepherd (illness) also practiced fully. Ruiz missed the Saints' game in Paris before the bye. Running back Alvin Kamara did not practice, although his absence was listed as rest-related, with a back designation. The Browns had several injury concerns on their first report, headlined by quarterback Deshaun Watson, who did not practice Wednesday while in the NFL's concussion protocol . Watson reported concussion symptoms following Cleveland's game against Pittsburgh and was subsequently placed in the protocol. His status for Sunday's matchup remains uncertain, leaving Shedeur Sanders as the potential replacement if Watson is unable to play. Cleveland had three other players listed as non-participants: defensive tackle Maliek Collins (elbow), linebacker Devin Williams (hamstring) and offensive lineman Alex Barber (calf). Five additional Browns were limited participants, including wide receiver David Boston (calf), cornerback Martin Harden (hamstring), center Ethan Jenkins (knee), linebacker Carson Schwesinger (wrist/ankle) and defensive end Jalen Verse (knee). Cleveland enters the week at 5-3, while New Orleans is 2-5.
