home.blurb: Sunday’s Week 9 matchup at the Caesars Superdome brings together two teams in very different positions, as the Cleveland Browns (5-3) take the field against the New Orleans Saints (2-5). Cleveland is third in the AFC North but just one game behind the first place Steelers. New Orleans has lost four of their last five games and sit last in the NFC South, but they are also only a game out of first as they return from their bye. The Superdome, however, has not been kind to the Saints who are winless in four home games (0-4). Cleveland, however, is a respectable 2-3 on the road this season. New Orleans has not played in a couple weeks, but their last game was also a loss to the Steelers, 16-10, in Paris on Oct. 25. The Saints managed only 18 rushing yards and were shut out in the second half, but quarterback Tyler Shough produced an encouraging performance through the air, completing 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards, one touchdown and one interception. It was symptomatic of the season to date: the offense has no balance. Historically, Cleveland leads the all-time series 13-7, but New Orleans has won each of the last three meetings, including the most recent matchup at this same venue on November 17, 2024. That game was tied 14-14 entering the fourth quarter before the Saints exploded for 21 unanswered points to win 35-14. Taysom Hill was the difference-maker, rushing seven times for 138 yards and three touchdowns, including fourth-quarter scoring runs of 33 and 75 yards, while Derek Carr threw for 248 yards and two touchdowns. Jameis Winston threw for 395 yards and two scores for Cleveland, but the Browns failed to turn their yardage into enough points. Two years later, the central question is similar for both clubs: which offense can translate production into touchdowns? Cleveland needs to protect Watson and rediscover a ground game that disappeared in Pittsburgh, while New Orleans needs Shough, Kamara and an offense coming out of the bye to take advantage of a Browns defense that just surrendered 200 rushing yards. Brown and Cam Jurgens for future draft picks. As for the Giants, who are in first place in the NFC East at 4-2-1, McCarthy has shined in his five quarters of action. The Eagles have lost six straight games, yet the team is resisting further change as it tries to navigate the rest of the season without Jalen Hurts. The Giants, meanwhile, have embraced adapting on the fly, most notably with the switch to J.J. McCarthy as the starting quarterback. McCarthy built a good deal of confidence in his first start with the Giants. After the bye, he could have an even more complete command of the offense, though Vic Fangio's defense could test his patience and precision. Is there any way up for an Eagles offense that has already reached rock bottom? Philadelphia ranks 30th in scoring and last in yards per game. Saquon Barkley has indicated he won't be dealt at the deadline, but even the 2024 Offensive Player of the Year looks incapable of rescuing this severely shorthanded crew. away.headline: Giants have uncertainty at running back going into their game at the Eagles
away.blurb: “I don't know,” the undrafted rookie said. “We're going to find out.” With Cam Skattebo nursing a hamstring injury, Tyrone Tracy out a month and Najee Harris gone after getting released, the Giants are down to just two healthy running backs on their roster and a couple more on the practice squad. Devin Singletary figures to shoulder the bulk of the load Sunday at Philadelphia, though the entire situation would change if they acquired Jonathan Taylor or another back before the weekend. “We’ve gotten better as the season’s went on, especially kind of made some big jumps recently,” said Bryan Hudson, who took over as the starting center beginning in Week 4 against Arizona. "Our attention to detail, execution and just doing all that through the week to get ready for game day I think is what has helped us do a good job and be consistent for the backs and just helping out whoever we got back there because we trust them, and we’re starting to build that trust to where they can trust us, too.” Linebacker Abdul Carter, whose role has gotten more substantial since Brian Burns was lost for the season with a knee injury, did not practice Wednesday because of an illness. Harbaugh expects Carter to be good to play Sunday. EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. (AP) — After the New York Giants claimed him off waivers last week, Greg Desrosiers is not sure what role awaits him in his first game with them. “I feel very confident about the running back situation,” coach John Harbaugh said after practice Wednesday. "I like the guys we’ve got, ... so I feel good about it. Harbaugh has made no secret of wanting an every-down runner like he had in Derrick Henry the previous two seasons with Baltimore. On Monday, he said any trade made that costs draft picks would have to benefit the organization beyond just this season. Taylor, the three-time Pro Bowl selection who has been one of the best backs in the NFL with Indianapolis for several years, happens to be under contract through 2028. He won't come cheap if the Colts opt to move him before the deadline Tuesday. Desrosiers did because New York poached him off the Los Angeles Chargers' practice squad. After bouncing around in college from Louisville to UMass to Memphis, the Boston area native was praying for an opportunity and may have gotten a bigger one than he even anticipated. “Hopefully I can come in and make plays and show my explosiveness and give them a reason to keep me here and show them why they chose me,” Desrosiers said. “I’ll promise this: I’m going to make it count.” Desrosiers could get a bunch of carries against the Eagles or be inactive or cut, depending on what roster moves happen between now and then. He's projecting confidence about how he'll perform if he plays, and so is the offensive line that paved the way for 188 yards on the ground Oct. 25 at Houston. “It's day to day," Harbaugh said. "Abdul should be fine. He's sick. He should be fine.” See AP’s full NFL coverage here

away.blurb: Starter Cam Skattebo on Wednesday did not practice, again working on the side with a rehab trainer as he deals with the hamstring injury he went down with on his 42-yard run down the stretch of the Week 7 overtime victory in Houston. It seems unlikely Skattebo will be able to play Sunday against the Eagles in Philadelphia. Mafah, 24, was a 2025 seven round draft pick of the Cowboys out of Clemson, where he played 50 games and ran for 2,887 yards and 28 touchdowns in four seasons. A bruiser at 6-foot-1 and 232 pounds, Mafah as a rookie spent time on injured reserve with a shoulder He got into one game for the Cowboys — against the Giants in Week 18 — and ran five times for 18 yards. After he was waived in late August, the Giants in mid-September signed him to their practice squad. Whether or not the Giants make a mega-trade to land Jonathan Taylor or Derrick Henry or are able to pull off a somewhat smaller deal, it sure looks as if the Giants need help at running back, as soon as possible. The Giants (4-2-1) are in first place in the NFC East. The Eagles (2-6) are in last place and riding a six-game losing streak. The Giants’ running back picture is bleak. Tyrone Tracy is currently on injured reserve with a strained hamstring and he will miss the next four games. That leaves Devin Singletary as the only NFL running back on the roster with any experience. Singletary was a healthy scratch in three consecutive games earlier this season before the eight-year veteran finished off the 27-21 victory over the Texans with a 30-yard touchdown run in OT. The only other running back on the roster is Greg Derosiers, signed Oct. 27 off the Chargers’ practice squad. Derosiers, 25, played at three colleges (Louisville, UMass, Memphis) and was not drafted. The Chargers signed him to their practice squad and, when Tracy was put on IR, the Giants signed Derosiers to their active roster. He has never appeared in an NFL game. The Giants two weeks ago signed to their practice squad Eric Gray, a running back they selected in the fifth round of the 2023 draft. Gray, 27, had 31 rushing attempts and 79 yards in 34 games the past three seasons. Gray had been on the Browns practice squad earlier this season. The other running back on the practice squad is Phil Mafah. When he picked up Derosiers, general manager Joe Schoen said he is a player “who we like.” As for Mafah, Schoen said “I’m excited to see what Greg can do.”

Giants Add Familiar Face at Running Back as Skattebo’s Injury Status Raises Questions Skip to main content SI.COM The New York Giants were back to work on Monday after their Week 8 bye, but one key offensive player worked with trainers on the sideline during the media portion of practice. Running back Cam Skattebo, who said he felt something in his hamstring after his 42-yard run against the Houston Texans in overtime two weeks ago, was spotted working to the side with trainers. It’s unclear whether Skattebo is simply trying to buy a couple more days to let his hamstring fully heal before the team begins its prep for Sunday’s road game at Philadelphia, or whether the injury could limit him in practice and, potentially, the upcoming game. Head coach John Harbaugh characterized Skattebo's status as "day to day." Either way, the Giants, who last week placed running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR with a hamstring injury, are not taking any chances of going into the critical division matchup with just Devin Singletary and newcomer Gregory Desrosiers, whom they signed last week off the Chargers’ practice squad. To that end, New York has signed running back Eric Gray, its fifth-round pick in the 2023 draft, to its practice squad. Gray, who was with the team this summer, appeared in 34 games over three seasons, including just four in 2025 after landing on PUP due to a knee injury. He has 31 career rushing attempts for 79 yards and caught 16 of 18 targets for 104 yards, with no rushing or receiving touchdowns. This past summer he led the team in receptions with eight catches for 54 yards. He also led the Giants in rushing with 90 yrds on 30 carries. Gray was with the Cleveland Browns practice squad in September but was released in early October. Devin Singletary figures to shoulder the bulk of the load Sunday at Philadelphia, though the entire situation would change if they acquired Jonathan Taylor or another back before the weekend. “We’ve gotten better as the season’s went on, especially kind of made some big jumps recently,” said Bryan Hudson, who took over as the starting center beginning in Week 4 against Arizona. "Our attention to detail, execution and just doing all that through the week to get ready for game day I think is what has helped us do a good job and be consistent for the backs and just helping out whoever we got back there because we trust them, and we’re starting to build that trust to where they can trust us, too.” Linebacker Abdul Carter, whose role has gotten more substantial since Brian Burns was lost for the season with a knee injury, did not practice Wednesday because of an illness. (AP) — After the New York Giants claimed him off waivers last week, Greg Desrosiers is not sure what role awaits him in his first game with them. “I feel very confident about the running back situation,” coach John Harbaugh said after practice Wednesday. "I like the guys we’ve got, ... so I feel good about it. Harbaugh has made no secret of wanting an every-down runner like he had in Derrick Henry the previous two seasons with Baltimore. away.headline: Rams Could Find Low-Cost, High-Reward Wide Receiver Solution in Brandon Aiyuk (But It's Complicated)
away.blurb: On Tuesday, another option potentially became available as San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk requested reinstatement from the NFL . Aiyuk hired Drew Rosenhaus to be his agent, who said that the wide receiver is healthy and ready to get back on the field. Over the summer, Aiyuk went on social media, calling out Shanahan and general manager John Lynch, effectively burning that bridge. Despite some interest from the Washington Commanders in the offseason, Aiyuk’s actions turned off Washington’s front office. “Sometimes you have to really ask yourself what kind of resources are you willing to give up?” McVay said on Monday. “I would never rule out opportunities to get better, but at what opportunity cost? You have to have another person that's willing to do it and you have to have somebody that you feel like would add a lot of value to your roster, and then what are the resources that you would be willing to give up when you're looking at it as a whole?” Again, this isn’t to say that the Rams need to sign Aiyuk, but just that it’s something they should explore if he becomes available. Aiyuk comes with obvious baggage, but he also brings a level of talent that rarely becomes available at this point in the season. The Rams benefitted from a similar situation in 2021 with Beckham. If the Rams can add an upgrade at a position of need without sacrificing draft capital, it's an opportunity worth considering. Aiyuk could be a low-risk, high-reward opportunity that Les Snead and McVay can't afford to overlook. As the Los Angeles Rams approach the NFL trade deadline, there’s no doubt that they are in need of a wide receiver . Without Davante Adams, the Rams have struggled with their receiver depth options outside of Puka Nacua. It’s possible that the Rams could look into making a trade for a player like Josh Downs or Brian Thomas Jr. However, with the market as competitive as it is at wide receiver, Downs and Thomas may require more draft capital than the Rams would want to give up. home.blurb: He joins fellow defensive tackle Daron Payne (foot) in being out for the season. Payne was placed on IR on Tuesday, four days after he sustained his injury during practice. Nov 04 (Field Level Media) - Washington Commanders defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw will miss the remainder of the season due to a knee injury, ESPN reported Wednesday. Kinlaw, 29, was placed on injured reserve Tuesday after he underwent surgery to repair an MCL injury. He sustained the injury during Washington's 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Oct. 19. Kinlaw recorded 13 tackles and one sack in six games (all starts) this season. Signed to a three-year deal prior to the 2025 season, Kinlaw has totaled 166 tackles, 10.5 sacks, three forced fumbles, one fumble recovery and an interception for a touchdown in 81 career games (68 starts) for the 49ers, New York Jets and Commanders. He was selected by San Francisco with the 14th overall pick of the 2020 NFL Draft.

With wins over the Commanders and the Cardinals over the next two weeks, the Rams could truly be back in contention. Getting both Garrett and Ferguson back on the field should only help Los Angeles going forward. away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The Denver Broncos returned to practice on Wednesday as they begin on-field preparations for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers . During the portion of Wednesday's practice that was open to media members, safeties Talanoa Hufanga ( ankle ) and Brandon Jones ( hamstring ) were both present . However, defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike ( shoulder ) and cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine ( ankle ) were not spotted at the indoor practice field. Hufanga has missed the team's last three games. Jones suffered a hamstring injury in practice last Thursday but was cleared to play in Sunday's game. He then aggravated the injury during a 28-24 win over the Kansas City Chiefs. Meanwhile, wide receiver Pat Bryant ( ankle ) returned to practice, opening his 21-day window to be activated from injured reserve. If Bryant is not activated within the next three weeks, he will spend the rest of the season on IR. Denver's scheduled to practice again on Thursday and Friday before releasing a final injury report with game statuses for Sunday's showdown with the Panthers . away.headline: Broncos WR Pat Bryant designated to return from injured reserve
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: Denver Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant ( ankle ) returned to practice on Wednesday, opening his 21-day window to return from injured reserve. If the Broncos do not activate Bryant to the 53-man roster within the next three weeks, he will remain on IR for the rest of the season. Bryant injured his ankle in Week 4 and sat out the team's last four games. Before that, he hauled in nine receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown. Once cleared to play again, Bryant will likely resume WR3 duties behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton in the second half of the season. NFL teams are allowed to designate up to eight players to return from injured reserve each season. Denver has already used three of those designations on offensive lineman Frank Crum ( leg ), tight end Caleb Lohner ( foot ) and running back Jonah Coleman, who returned in Week 7. Crum and Lohner have not yet returned to practice. away.headline: Texans lose WR Jaylin Noel to season-ending toe injury
away.blurb: According to multiple reports, the Houston Texans are placing Noel on the season-ending injured reserve after suffering a turf toe injury in Week 7's loss to the New York Giants . Houston's top big-play threat will not return for the rest of the regular season and perhaps the postseason, though sitting with a mere two wins doesn't seem promising for a playoff bid entering November. Noel also served as the team's primary return man on both kickoffs and punts, averaging over 11.0 yards per punt return. Now, Houston has weapons. Earlier this month, the Texans traded for Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Arizona Cardinals in exchange for a second-round pick. Last week against the Giants, Tank Dell return for the first time in nearly two years. Based on his timeline in Sunday's matchup, Noel suffered the injury with roughly nine minutes left in regulation after returning a kickoff from the Giants. Based on the report, he appeared to have twisted his toe on the turf and was seen leaving the stadium in a boot. In a corresponding move, the Texans claimed former Cowboys and Cardinals running back Emari Demercado off waivers after his release on Tuesday. He'll join the active roster once the team returns from the bye week. Not only is this a big blow for Noel's promising sophomore season, but it's a loss for the passing game in general. The former Iowa State was led the team with 331 receiving yards to go along with catches and two receiving touchdowns. Noel is the second Texans receiver and the second Iowa State pass-catcher to suffer a season-ending injury this year, joing second-round pick Jayden Higgins, who suffered a torn ACL in August. Dell had one catch for 43 yards on just 10 snaps. Harrison caught a touchdown pass on the same drive and only played in 14 snaps. Both will have a larger role when the team returns from the bye week to take on the Los Angeles Chargers. Across five games this season, he has taken the ball 52 times for only 138 yards, resulting in a poor 2.7 yards per carry. During Week 5, the free agent acquisition pulled his groin in a game at the Tennessee Titans. He has been sidelined since. On Monday, the Texans signed RB Joshua Pitsenberger to the practice squad, per Jonathan M Alexander of the Houston Chronicle. Moments after this transaction was reported, Houston head coach Demeco Ryans said he did not have any significant update on Montgomery's health. His status for Week 9 appears to be in jeopardy. Pitsenberger is a 2026 undrafted free agent whom the Texans signed briefly after the draft. He has yet to appear in an NFL game but now becomes the fifth running back on the team, active roster and practice squad included. Houston has three RBs on the active roster, that being Woody Marks, Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale. The offense this season has largely relied on the arm of quarterback C.J. Stroud. picks.blurb: Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:49 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is one of the most interesting and compelling games of the schedule for Week 9 and the first half of the NFL season. The Green Bay Packers are starting to find their offensive rhythm with Jordan Love improving on a week-by-week basis, but the team is still waiting for Micah Parsons to return to help the defense assert itself. The New England Patriots are in full stride at the moment. After losing two of their first three games and looking like last year's Super Bowl champions might take a step or two backwards, the Patriots have found their stride once again. It certainly begins with Drake Maye , who is starting to make a case as one of the NFL's elite quarterbacks, but it goes much deeper than that. The Patriots have been getting excellent play from their offensive line and running back Rhamondre Stevenson is one of the most dependable players that head coach Mike Vrabel has on his roster. His presence is a security blanket to the rest of the team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) While the Patriots are feeling better about themselves on an every-week basis, the defense is also getting the job done. New England ranks 9th in scoring defense , as the Patriots are giving up 20.3 points per game. However, the Packers may be encouraged when they look at the New England pass defense because that unit is only slightly better than average, ranking 13th in the league. Jordan Love will throw for 250 yards and 2 touchdowns The Packers would like to come at the Patriots with a balanced, versatile and unpredictable attack. The return of Josh Jacobs from the commissioner's exempt list gave head coach Matt LaFleur a solid option running the ball. However, recent allegations of additional domestic violence incidents against Jacobs could result in additional discipline by the NFL. While he is still eligible at this moment, LaFleur might want to bypass that portion of the gameplan. As a result, it will be on Love to direct a consistent offensive attack, and he will be under significant pressure from the Patriots' aggressive defense. Love is one of the best pure passers in the game, and if the offensive line gives him protection, he can drive the Green Bay attack. Love has completed 192 of 312 passes for 2,246 yards and is averaging 280.8 yards per game. He has thrown 16 TD passes and 6 interceptions. He has a trio of receivers who are likely to cause problems in Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and TE Tucker Kraft. Watson's speed, route running and dependable hands should help the Patriots stay in this vital road game. Look for Love to connect with Watson for at least one key touchdown in the fourth quarter. Maye will approach 225 passing yards and 2 touchdowns Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Look for Maye to be turned on to the maximum level for this matchup with Love. He knows that Love throws one of the best deep balls in the league, and Maye wants to compete with him in all areas. While Love is also a good runner who can escape the pass rush, Maye excels in that area. Look for Maye to show off those running skill early in the game, and that will force the Packers to employ a spy who will attempt to contain the quarterback. That's when Maye will start to show off his pinpoint passing. The Patriots quarterback has completed 157 of 234 passes for 1,983 yards with 15 touchdowns and 8 interceptions. In addition to those numbers, his confidence is sky high. While the Patriots have not gotten the production from former Eagles wideout A.J. Brown, he can depend on wide receiver DeMario Douglas and tight end Hunter Henry to show off their productivity against Green Bay's eighth-ranked pass defense. Stevenson will rush for 75-plus yards and 1 TD The Patriots have one of the most underrated running backs in the game in Rhamondre Stevenson. While he is not a gamebreaker in terms of speed, he understands all aspects of the game. He runs well between the tackles and he will finish off his rushing attempts with power. He knows how to set up his blockers and accelerate at the right moment. The Patriots have TreVeyon Henderson — when healthy — to show off his skills as a speed back. However, it is Stevenson who is a difference maker and will give the Patriots the edge they need to beat a solid opponent. Patriots will outlast Packers and earn 27-24 triumph The escape factor that Maye provides will allow him to buy extra time and create more plays for the Patriots. This will allow them to maintain possession and sustain their drives. He will also get a huge lift from Stevenson, who is simply a winner and will come through when the game is on the line. The Packers will push the Patriots to the limit, but the Pats will have the benefit of their homefield, as well as their two key difference makers. New England comes away with this exciting and well-played victory. After the receiver missed Sunday's win over the Dolphins with a knee injury, Mike Vrabel said Monday that the team would need to see how Brown progresses before determinig his status for the upcoming tilt. Micah Parsons is expected to make his much-anticipated return to practice this week for the Packers, but he might still be a long way out from contributing. Matt LaFleur said the edge rusher might need the full 21-day window before being added to the active roster, which would mean a late November return. If there is any change to running back Josh Jacobs' disciplinary status, it won't come from the Packers. LaFleur said this week that the team plans to continue on with the ball carrier as the NFL extends its investigation. Plus, Christian Watson is dealing with a rib injury that sent him to the hospital for a portion of last week's primetime win over the Panthers. The Pats have the personnel to take advantage defensively, but Maye's offense also has questions around injuries to A.J. Brown, Hunter Henry and others. I'll take New England at home, but I'm expecting nervous pacing around living rooms throughout Massachusetts before this one is settled. Between their reliance on Jordan Love connecting on vertical shots and the pass rush picking up the rest of the defense with pressure, Green Bay might be more reliant of the two on igniting big plays. But the Packers' explosiveness shouldn't be doubted, and it could lead the team to its fifth win in six games. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Packers 26, Patriots 23 Good luck figuring these teams out. Brown play for the Patriots? Does it matter? Drop issues have plagued the star receiver and there's no sign of that disappearing anytime soon. On the other side, Christian Watson made 'Thursday Night Football” look like the WWE with his dramatic return. In the end, we'll trust the Packers offense to be the difference. New England’s defense ranks ninth in points per game allowed (20.3) and 11th in third-down defense (38.5%). The Patriots’ last three wins have come over the Dolphins, Jets, and Raiders, and they only have two wins against teams with a winning record (BUF, PIT). away.blurb: GREEN BAY — Micah Parsons is practicing again with the Green Bay Packers as the All-Pro edge rusher approaches a return from the torn anterior cruciate ligament that has sidelined him since mid-December. Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Wednesday that Parsons would be participating in individual drills. Parsons’ return to practice means the Packers have 21 days before they need to activate him from injured reserve. “It’s been a long time coming,” LaFleur said. “He’s put a lot of effort and work into this. The team says Nixon is questionable to play with a shoulder injury. Nixon joins four other questionable players for the Packers: receiver Matthew Golden (foot/shoulder), defensive linemen Anthony Campbell (ankle) and Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and edge rusher Brenton Cox Jr. (quad). Linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and right guard Travis Glover (knee) have all been ruled out for Thursday night. away.headline: Is Matthew Golden playing tonight? Injury update for Packers WR
away.blurb: The 23-year-old had originally been listed as "questionable" due to shoulder and foot injuries, but he was able to suit up for his eighth game of the season. Golden logged a "limited" practice session on Wednesday after being listed as a non-participant in both Monday's estimated injury report and Tuesday's actual practice session. Packers coach Matt LaFleur was asked whether Golden would be available Thursday during a news conference on Tuesday, Oct. 27. LaFleur also pointed out that the nature of the short week would lead to most sessions being a walkthrough, so his players wouldn't get "any real reps" in advance of the game. The Green Bay Packers are preparing to take on the Carolina Panthers on " Thursday Night Football " in Week 8, marking the second time they have played an NFC South team on a short week this season. This time around, there are questions about whether the Packers will have one of their top wide receivers, Matthew Golden , at their disposal for the game. Golden is dealing with shoulder and foot injuries that have cast doubt on his availability for Thursday's game against the Packers. Golden has appeared in all seven Packers games so far in 2026. He has enjoyed a breakout season, tallying 36 catches for 540 yards and three touchdowns, though he has committed a league-high six drops. Here's what to know about Golden's status for the Packers' Week 8 game against the Panthers and how Green Bay may replace him if he cannot play. Is Matthew Golden playing tonight? Golden is officially active for the Packers' Week 8 "Thursday Night Football" matchup against the Panthers. Golden playing isn't a major surprise. NFL Media's Ian Rapoport provided a positive update on the second-year receiver during a Thursday, Oct. 29, appearance on "Good Morning Football." "I'm told he's trending towards playing," Rapoport said . "So, there's a good chance for the Packers that Matthew Golden does get on the field today." "I sure hope so," LaFleur responded . "But again, we're still kind of working through it." "We will have a short indie tomorrow, but to move guys around to see how they look," LaFleur said, describing the team's practice procedures. "But certainly hopeful for [Golden]." Who is Matthew Golden's backup? J. Michael Sturdivant is listed as Golden's primary backup on the Packers' official depth chart . The undrafted rookie from Florida has played sparingly through six games, notching three catches for 22 yards, all of which came in Green Bay's Week 3 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. But while Sturdivant is listed as Golden's backup, Savion Williams and Bo Melton have each logged more snaps than the Florida product. As such, those two may be more likely to fill in for Golden across from Christian Watson if the former Texas star can't play. Patriots WR coach Todd Downing shares his thoughts on A.J. Brown On Thursday, New England Patriots WR coach Todd Downing spoke with the media. While discussing A.J. The Niners are big favorites in a game that's expected to be high-scoring. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , San Francisco opened up as 9.5-point favorites with the total set at 51.5. That ties for the highest total this season and the second-largest point spread. Raiders games have been video game-esque. They just beat the Jets 38-33. They let the Rams score 35 in Week 7. The Bills scored 33 in Week 6, and Drake Maye dropped 45 the week prior. Geno Smith threw for 290 yards. Adonai Mitchell was unguardable, while Garrett Wilson had a "quiet" 83 yards. It was a different story against the Rams. Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each ran for over 90 yards. Let's just say the 49ers aren't going up against the 2000 Ravens. Kirk Cousins, who threw three touchdowns, has no problem tossing it up to Bowers in contested situations. Bowers has double-digit targets in all but two games this season. He's a monster, so you understand why Vegas goes out of their way to feature him. The 49ers haven't covered the spread in a couple of weeks. They've also gone under the total in back-to-back weeks. picks.headline: Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions for NFL Week 9
picks.blurb: Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:56 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Las Vegas Raiders arrive at Levi's Stadium with renewed confidence. The San Francisco 49ers arrive with extra rest and something to prove. Las Vegas snapped a four-game losing streak with a 38–33 victory over the Jets, improving to 4–4. San Francisco, meanwhile, returns from its bye at 6–1 after suffering its first defeat, a 29–20 loss to Atlanta. Their November 8 matchup offers a test of whether the Raiders' rebound represents progress or another temporary escape. The opening market favors San Francisco by 10 points, with a total of 51.5. These predictions envision something more explosive than that total suggests: a quarterback showcase, a monster receiving performance and a decisive fourth-quarter separation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brock Purdy throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Purdy will deliver his most convincing statistical statement of the season, reaching 350 passing yards and throwing four touchdown passes. That projection starts with a favorable matchup. Las Vegas has surrendered at least 30 points in five consecutive games, allowing opponents to dictate too many possessions. Even Sunday's victory required the Raiders to overcome 33 points from the Jets. Purdy already has 1,748 passing yards and 15 touchdowns through seven games. Before the bye, he threw for 288 yards against Atlanta despite injuries affecting several important offensive contributors. The Raiders should expect Kyle Shanahan to test their coverage communication immediately. Motion, play-action and layered routes can create uncertainty without requiring Purdy to hold the ball for extended periods. My projection anticipates San Francisco attacking through the air even after establishing a lead. Rather than leaning exclusively on clock management, Shanahan will keep exploiting favorable matchups. Brock Bowers produces 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns The Raiders' best answer will come through Brock Bowers, who will turn a difficult road assignment into a dominant individual performance. The prediction is at least 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including one reception covering 40 or more yards. That would require Las Vegas to build its passing plan around Bowers rather than waiting for him to emerge naturally within the progression. Quick throws would establish his involvement, while crossing routes and seam opportunities would provide the bigger gains. Kirk Cousins enters the matchup following a three-touchdown performance against the Jets, and his recent play has kept rookie Fernando Mendoza on the sideline. That continuity matters for this prediction. The Raiders can attack with an experienced quarterback rather than simplifying everything around a developmental transition. The projected game script should also create volume. If San Francisco scores early, Las Vegas will need to maintain an aggressive passing approach rather than protect field position. Bowers would become the central answer, particularly on third downs and near the goal line. His production will keep the Raiders competitive longer than expected, even as their defense struggles to match it. The teams combine for 70 points as San Francisco wins 42–28 The final prediction is a shootout that eventually becomes a comfortable 49ers victory. A 42–28 result would produce 70 total points, sailing past the opening 51.5-point total while giving San Francisco a 14-point winning margin. The logic connects the first two bold predictions, Purdy repeatedly punishes defensive breakdowns, while Cousins and Bowers generate enough offense to prevent an early rout. Ultimately, the difference will be possession-to-possession consistency. Las Vegas will manufacture explosive moments, but San Francisco will sustain more scoring drives and turn one late Raiders mistake into the decisive touchdown. The Raiders will show offensive resilience. The 49ers will show why their ceiling remains substantially higher. The Niners sit atop the NFC West while the Raiders sit third in the AFC West but just a single game out of the final playoff position. The Raiders snapped a four-game losing streak last Sunday rallying for a 38-33 win over the Jets in New York. Kirk Cousins threw for 247 yards and three touchdowns. Brock Bowers caught seven balls including two for touchdowns and Mike Washington Jr. ran for 83 yards. Cousins has been a bit of a revelation for the Raiders playing better than he has in the past couple of years. The veteran has thrown for 2,124 yards including 19 touchdowns against only five interceptions. Somewhat under the radar, the 49ers return from their bye week with a three-game lead in what was billed in the preseason as the best division in the NFL. When last we saw San Francisco, the Niners were on the short end of a 29-20 game against the Falcons. Brock Purdy was an MVP candidate last season and is back in the mix this season having thrown for 1,748 yards including 15 touchdowns and only four interceptions. Christian McCaffrey is having another banner season, rushing for 389 yards and catching Purdy passes for 251 yards. San Francisco is still a MASH unit on defense, but DeForest Buckner is expected to suit up for his first game back with his original team after being acquired last week from the Colts. This rivalry’s history is remarkably close: the 49ers own an 8-7 edge in 15 regular-season meetings. Sunday’s revival of the rivalry carries considerably more than regional nostalgia: Las Vegas can continue their surprising playoff push and climb above .500 with an upset, while San Francisco has an opportunity to respond to its first loss, protect its unbeaten home record and reinforce its position atop a competitive NFC West. The matchup marks the 16th meeting between the two teams and the first time the Raiders have visited the 49ers for a regular-season game since relocating to Las Vegas following the 2019 season. San Francisco is looking to earn its third consecutive victory over the Raiders and improve to 9-7 all-time against the franchise. How has this series played out historically? The 49ers entered their bye week following a loss to the Atlanta Falcons. On offense, QB Brock Purdy completed 27 of 40 pass attempts for 288 yards and one touchdown. RB Christian McCaffrey recorded seven carries for 39 yards and a touchdown, along with six receptions for 61 yards. Rookie RB Kaelon Black added 12 carries for a team-high 63 yards and scored his first rushing touchdown. FB Kyle Juszczyk caught three passes for 11 yards, including a one-yard touchdown reception. Defensively, the 49ers held the Falcons to 82 rushing yards. LB Fred Warner led the team with 14 tackles and added one forced fumble. The 49ers Communications staff provided the above breakdown. Below is everything you need to know to follow the upcoming game. Sunday, November 8 at 1:25 p.m. PT Where is the game being played? Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California As of November 4, the 49ers are favored by 10 points in this game, with an over/under set at 52.5 points, per BetMGM. Fans can listen at 49ers.com/esp . Las Vegas area fans can listen on KOMP 92.3 FM and KRLV 920 AM, where Jason Horowitz and Kirk Morrison will call the game. Fans can listen to the game on Compass Media, where Troy Clardy and Brian Baldinger will call the game. Fans can discuss the game within our Niner Talk forum . While there isn’t much positivity about the Seattle Seahawks from fans following the team’s blowout loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday, that hasn’t slowed confidence from oddsmakers ahead of their Week 9 game. According to the current odds on FanDuel Sportsbook , the Seahawks enter their second game against the Arizona Cardinals as 10.5-point favorites (-110) , with Seattle’s moneyline is set at -650 , while Arizona’s sits at +480 . The over/under line for the game is 44.5 , indicating that the Seahawks, now 4-4, are more than likely headed for another defensive slogfest against the Cardinals. The man trusted to score those points for the Cardinals will be none other than Washington State alum Gardner Minshew, who brought his patented good vibes to Arizona in the team’s second-half upset of the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. Minshew ignited a spark in the Cardinals’ offense, which helped them score the most points, 33, that they’ve scored in a game all year. Arizona’s gutsy win in overtime against the Dallas Cowboys lifted them to 3-5 on the season. Aside from Minshew, running back Tyler Allgier had a career day after taking over for rookie Jeremiyah Love. The journeyman quarterback’s favorite target was Michael Wilson, who willed his team to a win with two broken ribs. The health of Wilson may be paramount to the Cardinals’ offense as he offers a second option for Minshew when superstar tight end Trey McBride is covered. While the Cardinals beat up on a reeling Cowboys’ defense, a trip to Seattle to play Mike Macdonald’s unit is an entirely different story. This unit held the Cardinals to 7 points in Week 2 and stifled much of Arizona’s run game. However, the story of these two teams’ early meeting was the Seahawks’ offense, which totaled 24 points in the second half after a slow start. Seattle, which was led by Drew Lock at the time, was led by their offensive engine, Jaxon Smith-Njigba. JSN totaled three touchdowns and 155 yards in that game, a performance the struggling Seahawks would love to see again. Unlike most of their games in 2026, the Seahawks had success on the ground in Week 2 with Emmanuel Wilson running for 92 yards and rookie Jadarian Price adding 52 yards. With Zach Charbonnet back, this matchup looks on paper to be the perfect bounce-back after they struggled to do much of anything on the ground against Chicago. With the pressure turned up on the .500 Seahawks, the oddsmakers appear to predict they’ll storm back with a win over their underdog story division rivals. away.headline: Jacoby Brissett traded to Ravens amid Lamar Jackson injury, latest NFL rumors on deal with Cardinals
away.blurb: For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . After losing star quarterback Lamar Jackson to a thumb injury and backup Tyler Huntley to a toe injury, the Baltimore Ravens reportedly made a much-needed addition. Per ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, the Ravens are finalizing a trade to acquire veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. The deal is expected to be completed this weekend. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

away.headline: Ravens acquire Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals after injuries to both Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley: report
away.blurb: The Ravens will start undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano on Thursday night against the Jaguars, but even he isn’t fully healthy. Fagnano suffered an ankle injury and was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report but was upgraded to a full participant on Tuesday. The Baltimore Ravens have help on the way. After superstar quarterback Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler "Snoop" Huntley suffered injuries in the team’s 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, the Ravens are acquiring quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals, according to ESPN. Because the Ravens play the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night, the trade will not be finalized until the weekend, according to the report. While Fagnano will start on Thursday, Brissett is expected to make his Ravens debut when they play the Los Angeles Chargers on "Monday Night Football" in Week 10. In place of Jackson and Huntley, Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and an interception. Brissett started all eight games for the Cardinals before being benched for Gardner Minshew II with Arizona trailing 17-3 in the third quarter of its 33-30 comeback victory over the Dallas Cowboys in overtime. With Brissett at the helm, the Cardinals were 2-5 this season. He completed 63.3% of his passes for 1,719 yards with 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. The Ravens will be the seventh team he has played for, and Baltimore hopes Brissett can keep the team in the playoff race. With their loss to the Bills on Sunday, the Ravens dropped to 4-4 and fell to last place in the AFC North. Jackson suffered a thumb injury that may potentially require season-ending surgery, while Huntley has a turf toe injury. The Ravens head into their matchup against the 5-2 Jaguars as massive underdogs with Fagnano as the starting quarterback . Baltimore hosts Jacksonville at 8:15 p.m. ET at M&T Bank Stadium on Thursday. away.headline: Ravens to trade for Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals to fill QB void: Report
away.blurb: Ravens to trade for QB Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals: Report – NBC New York Skip to content Breaking Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to potential season-ending injuries last week. By Logan Reardon • Published 16 minutes ago • Updated 16 minutes ago Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. There's a new quarterback in Baltimore. Days after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley suffered potential season-ending injuries , the Ravens reportedly traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the news on Wednesday, adding that the trade is expected to be finalized over the weekend. Watch NBC 4 free wherever you are With the Ravens playing on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the earliest that Brissett could make his debut for the team would be on Monday, Nov. 16, against the Los Angeles Chargers . Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start for Baltimore against Jacksonville, with inexperienced quarterbacks Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis serving as the backups. Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and two turnovers in his relief debut Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after Jackson and Huntley went down. The two-time MVP Jackson, coming off three missed games with an ankle injury, suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery on his first throw last Sunday. His backup, Huntley, returned to the field, but he went down with a turf toe injury that will require surgery in the second quarter. Brissett, 33, lost his starting job to Gardner Minshew on Sunday. That made him an obvious trade candidate before next Tuesday's deadline, and the Ravens pounced quickly. Brissett started Arizona's first eight games this season and went 3-5 with 1,719 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Detroit Lions star Jack Campbell says he has ‘full movement' of lower body after scary on-field injury Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol as Shedeur Sanders could start for Browns An 11-year NFL veteran, Brissett has several ties to the Ravens' coaching staff. Quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork held the same position for the Cardinals last season and passing game coordinator Marcus Brady was a Colts assistant when Brissett was there from 2018-20. Brissett was drafted in 2016 by the New England Patriots and has gone on to play for six teams before Baltimore -- the Patriots (2016, 2024), Indianapolis Colts (2017-20), Miami Dolphins (2021), Cleveland Browns (2022), Washington Commanders (2023) and Cardinals (2025-26). The Seahawks don't currently have any other quarterbacks on the roster. Macdonald didn't rule out the possibility of adding another signal caller ahead of Sunday's game. The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos. Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs. Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will be sidelined with a quad injury for Sunday's matchup against the visiting Arizona Cardinals, head coach Mike Macdonald announced Wednesday. Darnold is considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald. Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of Monday's loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald. Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions. Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold. Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can." As of Wednesday, Macdonald said Lock was "able to throw" but that his capacity would be determined during practice this week. Milroe has yet to see game action this season. home.headline: ‘Best Silent Benching Ever,’ ‘They Play Better With the Backup’ — NFL Fans React to Seahawks Ruling Out Sam Darnold With Injury for Week 9
home.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks will be without Sam Darnold for Sunday’s Week 9 home game against the Arizona Cardinals after coach Mike Macdonald ruled the quarterback out Wednesday with a quad injury, though some fans suspect Seattle is sitting Darnold for his performance rather than his health. Macdonald, however, laid out a different explanation and a timeline: “Sam injured his quad at the end of the game, so Sam’s going to be out this week. It’s going to be week to week for Sam.” The Seahawks also aren’t placing Darnold on injured reserve, so a return as soon as the Nov. 15 trip to the Las Vegas Raiders remains possible. The news arrives with the defending Super Bowl champions at 4-4 following Monday night’s 34-17 home loss to the Chicago Bears, and it sends Seattle back to Drew Lock, who finished the season opener after Darnold suffered what was later diagnosed as a glute injury on Seattle’s opening possession. This time, however, Lock is in line to start while dealing with his own elbow injury. Fans See a Benching Behind Sam Darnold’s Quad Injury The theory follows a Monday night in which Darnold threw all 34 of Seattle’s passes, completing 17 for 188 yards with two touchdowns and an interception while taking three sacks. That interception, by James Lynch with 6:01 left in the fourth quarter, gave Chicago the ball at the Seattle 6 and set up the touchdown that made it 34-17. Darnold’s 79.5 passer rating through Week 8 ranks 26th of 31 qualified quarterbacks, and he has thrown nine interceptions to go with 10 touchdown passes. Pro Football Network’s NFL QB Impact Grade has him at 71.5 through Week 8, 21st of 35 graded quarterbacks. One fan took the theory a step further: “Soft benching. Darnold never sees the field again as a Seahawk. Biggest liability in football.” Lock hasn’t played in the last two games because of his elbow, and he was listed only as the emergency third quarterback on Monday while Jalen Milroe served as Darnold’s No. 2. Milroe is slated to back up Lock on Sunday, and Macdonald stood behind both: “We have full confidence in those guys and will have a plan in place.” The injury label itself caught flak from another fan , who wrote, “‘Quad injury’ is the best silent benching ever.” One fan widened the theory beyond Seattle: “First it’s Sam Darnold, then it’s Kyler Murray. The soft benchings are underway.” Holden Cantor, a Los Angeles Rams content creator, reached the same conclusion more bluntly, writing, “He got benched.” Drew Lock’s Two September Games Put the Backup in the Conversation While most of the reaction cast the injury as cover for a benching, a second line of thinking focused on what Seattle looked like without Darnold. away.headline: Buccaneers' Yaya Diaby suffers Grade 2 MCL sprain
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, Diaby suffered a Grade 2 MCL sprain and is expected to miss time, although a return within a matter of weeks is possible. Head coach Todd Bowles confirmed Monday that Diaby sprained his MCL and said he hopes he will avoid injured reserve. Diaby exited in the first quarter and did not return to the Week 8 contest. The official NFL gamebook shows he played just seven of Tampa Bay's 53 defensive snaps (13%), forcing the Buccaneers to adjust their edge rotation. The injury interrupts Diaby's momentum after he recorded three sacks for 21 lost yards against Carolina in Week 7. Tampa Bay managed to shut out Atlanta without recording a sack, relying instead on four interceptions from Michael Penix Jr. No official return date has been announced. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost edge rusher Yaya Diaby to a knee injury during Sunday's 16-0 shutout of the Atlanta Falcons, and the latest reports indicate he could miss multiple games. Rookie Rueben Bain Jr. led the group with 35 snaps (66%), followed by David Walker with 25 (47%), Al-Quadin Muhammad with 23 (43%), and Anthony Nelson with 16 (30%). Diaby's potential absence creates an opportunity for Walker, who leads Tampa Bay with four sacks, and Bain to take on additional responsibilities. The Buccaneers face Chicago in Week 9 before their bye, giving them an extra week to recover before their next game. home.blurb: Cole Kmet is out for the season. Colston Loveland has shown plenty of promise , but expecting the rookie to handle everything Kmet brought to Ben Johnson's offense isn't particularly realistic. The concern is what Philadelphia would demand in return. It would be a shame to watch an offense this talented become limited by something Poles had an opportunity to address before the deadline. Bears veteran is running out of excuses after latest blockbuster trade The Chicago Bears have a 6-2 record , an offense that just embarrassed Seattle and a rather inconvenient problem at tight end. Now, with the November 10th trade deadline approaching, Ryan Poles has a decision to make . Does he trust the players already on the roster, or does he spend another draft pick to give Caleb Williams some help? Mike Moraitis Sports Illustrated has identified three potential trade candidates who could address Chicago's sudden lack of depth. Bears have three different options to replace Cole Kmet In Moraitis' report, he suggested that Dallas Goedert, Mo Alie-Cox and Luke Schoonmaker were identified as possible trade options for Chicago. None would be a direct replacement for everything Kmet provided. That's the problem Poles has to sort through. Kmet caught just 10 passes for 87 yards and a touchdown before suffering his season ending knee injury against New England. Those numbers hardly suggest Chicago lost a major receiving weapon. But Kmet's job involved considerably more than catching passes. He helped open running lanes, handled blocking assignments and allowed Johnson to use multiple tight end formations without making the offense predictable. Loveland can certainly catch the football. Asking him to absorb all of those responsibilities while continuing to develop as a receiver is another story. Rookie Sam Roush has stepped into a larger role, but Chicago is putting considerable faith in two young tight ends during a season when expectations have changed dramatically. That's why another veteran makes sense. Dallas Goedert offers the most proven receiving ability Goedert would give Williams another established target, particularly on third downs and in the red zone. The Philadelphia Eagles veteran has spent years producing in an offense that expects its tight ends to contribute as receivers and blockers. He's also playing on an expiring contract, making him an intriguing short term option. Chicago already spent heavily to acquire Simmons. Giving up another valuable draft pick for a player who could leave after the season wouldn't be particularly appealing. Mo Alie-Cox could be the better fit for Chicago Alie-Cox isn't going to sell many jerseys or make headlines with spectacular receiving numbers. He might be exactly what Johnson needs, though. The Indianapolis Colts veteran has built his reputation around physical blocking and doing the work that rarely shows up in a box score. Can the Buffalo Bills keep rolling against the NFL's stingiest defense? Can the Minnesota Vikings generate enough offense to avoid wasting another strong defensive performance? Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9 following a 36–10 victory over Baltimore. Minnesota returns home after Detroit ended its unbeaten start with a 19–15 win. The Bills opened as three-point favorites, setting up a compelling clash between offensive firepower and defensive disruption. These three predictions anticipate a departure from Minnesota's usual defensive script, explosive passing, costly mistakes and a dramatic finish that hands Buffalo its second defeat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Justin Jefferson explodes for 175 yards and two touchdowns Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Jefferson will deliver the performance Minnesota has been waiting for, finishing with at least 175 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Jefferson caught five passes for 33 yards and a touchdown against Detroit and enters Week 9 without a 100-yard receiving game. Buffalo presents an opportunity to change that. Its defense ranks 30th against the pass, making this a matchup Minnesota should attack rather than approach conservatively. The Vikings need to manufacture touches before asking Jefferson to win difficult downfield assignments. Motion, condensed formations and crossing routes would help create cleaner releases and give the quarterback defined throwing windows. The bigger gains should follow when Buffalo adjusts to those shorter completions. One double move or broken coverage could turn a productive evening into a spectacular one. Quarterback availability remains important. Kyler Murray is managing hamstring tightness , with Carson Wentz the likely alternative if Murray cannot play. Expect Minnesota to make its best receiver the centerpiece, not merely a name opponents must account for. Josh Allen accounts for four touchdowns but commits three turnovers Allen will produce enough spectacular plays to keep Buffalo dangerous and enough mistakes to give Minnesota control of the outcome. The bold prediction is four total touchdowns alongside three turnovers, including at least two interceptions. https://twitter.com/search?q=josh%20allen&src=typed_query&f=top Minnesota's defense provides the foundation for that aggressive forecast. Entering Week 9, the Vikings lead the league in points allowed per game at 13.3, quarterback pressure rate at 45.8 percent and sack percentage at 10.96 percent. Pressure alone will not neutralize Allen. His ability to escape the pocket can turn a successful blitz into a defensive emergency, particularly when coverage players must chase receivers across the field. That creates the central tension. Minnesota will win several snaps decisively, but Allen will punish a few failed pressure attempts with explosive completions or scrambling opportunities. The turnovers will come when he tries to rescue plays that should end with a throwaway. Disguised coverage behind an apparent blitz can invite exactly that kind of aggressive decision. Buffalo's offensive line also bears watching. Right tackle Spencer Brown's availability is a concern entering the matchup, potentially complicating protection against Minnesota's pressure packages. Allen will remain the game's most dangerous improviser. On this night, improvisation will carry a substantial price. Minnesota wins 38–35 on a last-second field goal The final bold prediction ties those individual performances together: Minnesota wins a shootout with a field goal as time expires. A 38–35 result would produce 73 points, comfortably exceeding the opening total of 46.5. It would also represent a dramatic departure from the Vikings' defensive scoring average. The logic is not that Minnesota suddenly becomes a bad defense. Turnovers and explosive plays can produce points without requiring long, methodical drives. Jefferson's breakout keeps the Vikings moving, while Allen repeatedly answers before one late mistake gives Minnesota the deciding possession. After losing its unbeaten record, Minnesota will respond with its most convincing offensive statement and a victory that reinforces its place among the league's contenders. picks.blurb: Two 6-1 teams, one marquee matchup. The Bills visit Minnesota after beating the Ravens 36-10, while the Vikings look to rebound from their first loss, a 19-15 defeat in Detroit. Kyler Murray's hamstring is the biggest injury to watch. Kevin O'Connell said Murray remained under evaluation Monday. Carson Wentz is the next option if Murray cannot play but, even if he starts, his mobility deserves attention. Wentz guided the Vikings to wins over the Packers and Bears in September, completing 59% of his passes with three touchdowns and no interceptions. Minnesota's protection is another concern. Left tackle Christian Darrisaw is dealing with shoulder soreness. His availability becomes especially important if Murray's hamstring limits his ability to escape pressure. Josh Allen's supporting cast needs monitoring, too. Joshua Palmer injured his hamstring against Baltimore, DJ Moore picked up another injury concern, and right tackle Spencer Brown missed that game with a back issue. Their practice participation will matter this week. The early market favors Buffalo on the road. The Bills are favorites of -3/-3.5 points, depending on where you do your shopping, and the total has dropped from 48.5 at open to as low as 45.5. Murray's status could move both numbers. If you're curious to read a couple of interesting trends: The Vikings are a perfect 7-0 SU and ATS in the fourth quarter this season, while the Bills are 6-0-1 SU and 7-0 ATS in the second quarter. These are shocking stats when you consider the teams are a combined 12-2 on the year, but just thought we'd pass it along. Whether it's Murray or Carson Wentz stepping in for him again, I still trust the Bills more to manufacture points. Brian Flores and the Vikings defense will make Allen work for everything – as the Lions just experienced in their low-scoring win – but the visitors simply have more at their disposal and I like them to remain unbeaten on the road. If the Bills can get Murray off schedule, it could be a difficult evening for Minnesota. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Vikings 21, Bills 16 Offense or defense? It was the Lions offense that triumphed against the Vikings defense, but there's reason to believe things could be different this week. Buffalo has been much looser with the football this year, turning it over 11 times – which ranks 11th-most in the league, while Detroit has the third-fewest. Suddenly, you see the Vikings' path to victory. Brian Flores' defense forces Josh Allen into a mistake or two on Monday night and that is the difference. home.blurb: Buffalo selected defensive tackle Zane Durant in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Penn State. He was expected to be a depth option for Buffalo, but he's been out injured. "I've seen him out at practice; he's in a jersey, no pads, and he's still on injured reserve. To me, it's kind of like the Bills are pretty healthy at defensive tackle right now, so I don't know if there is a road for him to make his return," Parrino said on The Shout! Podcast . "Look, I'm just watching it out there, but I think the silent tape's going to speak loudly [on Monday] in terms of the way that they played for one another, the way they ran around, the communication. Everything we challenged them with coming off the bye, I thought they responded to it, and they just kept going." The Buffalo Bills are unlikely to get back a rookie defensive player anytime soon. The Bills are off to a 6-1 start and will play the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football. Buffalo Bills Get Injury Update on Zane Durant In preseason and training camp, Durant flashed his potential, and many fans thought he would make an impact. However, Durant was placed on injured reserve at the end of August due to a neck stinger. He's been on the practice field, but Bills insider Matt Parrino of NYUP.com said he wasn't sure if Durant gets activated this year. Durant played four years at Penn State and was a big part of their defense. In his final season, he recorded 25 tackles, 4 sacks, and an interception . The Bills' defense has been an issue this season, but on Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens , they looked much better. After watching back the tape, Bills head coach Joe Brady said that is how the defense is expected to play every week. "I think our defense should look at today and understand that that's what the expectation is," Brady said . "And I'm not talking about the production. I'm not talking about the takeaways and sacks. I'm talking about the style that they played, the way that they flew around. The Bills defense will now go up against the struggling Vikings offense. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his three-week window opened to return from IR this week but will not return this week. Starting slot cornerback Roger McCreary was a late addition to the Lions' injury report on Friday, when he was limited with a foot injury. He is questionable for Sunday's game, which means he's likely to play. For the Vikings, close to a clean sheet with just a late addition of Jay Ward to the injury report on Friday with knee issue. He was limited on Friday and listed as questionable, but again that means he's likely to play. So, looks like full rosters will be available for both teams on Sunday, except for those on IR.
